author: Haoke98
body:
## Summary

Some aarch64 VMs (and some emulated/sandboxed CPU models) list `sve`/`sve2`/`sme` in `AT_HWCAP` while faulting on the first SVE instruction. OpenSSL's aarch64 cpuprobe derives the vector length by executing `cntb` at library load, so the fault lands during import and the process dies with `SIGILL` before it can log or report anything — it reads as a random startup crash in whatever imported OpenSSL-backed code (`cryptography`, `jwt`, `ssl` via a bundled OpenSSL) first.

`OPENSSL_armcap=0` makes OpenSSL skip the probe and use its portable paths. The cost is ARM hardware crypto acceleration, which is the right trade against not starting at all.

The guard probes a throwaway child with the variable stripped and acts **only** when that child was killed by `SIGILL`, so a missing module or any other ordinary failure never disables hardware crypto. Probing beats reading `AT_HWCAP` because whether the crash happens also depends on the OpenSSL build in the running interpreter: on the host this was reported from, the 3.11 environment imports `cryptography` fine while the 3.13 one dies.

It runs beside `_early_recovery` in `hermes_cli/main.py`, before the first OpenSSL-backed import anywhere below; `_openssl_arm_guard` is stdlib-only for that reason. No-op off aarch64 Linux and when `OPENSSL_armcap` is already configured, partial masks included.

## What does this PR do?

Adds a startup guard that detects — by direct experiment, not by trusting CPU feature bits — whether this interpreter's OpenSSL dies with `SIGILL` while loading, and sets `OPENSSL_armcap=0` when it does.

The failure mode cannot be handled from inside the process that hits it: the signal is raised at dynamic-library load, so there is no exception to catch and nothing gets a chance to log. The guard therefore shells out to one throwaway child, inheriting the environment with `OPENSSL_armcap` removed, and inspects only its exit status. `-signal.SIGILL` is the sole evidence that triggers action; a clean exit, a non-zero exit from a missing module, a timeout, or a missing interpreter are all treated as "no evidence" and leave hardware crypto enabled.

This is why it is a probe rather than an `AT_HWCAP` check: the advertised bits are precisely the thing that lies, and the same faulty host can crash on one interpreter and work on another depending on which OpenSSL/cryptography build is loaded.

## Related Issue

No existing issue — found while debugging a startup crash on a
title: fix(cli): survive aarch64 hosts that advertise SVE they cannot execute

author: liorzilp
body:
## Summary

The exhausted-turn chat copy (`agent/turn_failure_copy.py`) advised **"switch models with /model"** unconditionally. Two real-world failure modes, observed on a single-provider deployment (corporate router, all routes behind one quota):

1. **Advice that cannot change the outcome** — 7 "switch models with /model" messages in 4 days during a 429 storm, with every routable model behind the same exhausted quota.
2. **A command that may be refused anyway** (busy / stale-checkout guards), so the copy can advertise a door the gateway itself keeps locked.

## Semantics (v4, final)

`exhausted_copy(..., viable_switch=...)` renders the switch clause only when `viable_switch` is True, computed at the exhaustion site (`max_retries_exhausted_result` in `agent/turn_recovery.py`) via the new `switch_advice_viable()`. **Default = keep the hint.** Withhold requires POSITIVE STRUCTURAL PROOF, both of:

1. **Account-envelope evidence, not the reason alone**: the failure is `rate_limit` AND carries a LONG structured reset window (`reset_seconds >= 120` — the same horizon at which the copy itself stops saying "wait a minute", #89401). Generic RPM/TPM/concurrency 429s and short-reset burst throttles are model-scoped in practice: a sibling deployment works, so the hint stays.
2. **Same-credential-surface proof for the configured detour path**: every `fallback_providers` entry shares the failed route's credential surface, decided via `agent.backend_identity.same_credential_surface` (single identity owner, labels never compared inline — #22548 lesson). A cross-surface hop keeps the hint; empty/malformed chains keep it (no proof).

Billing never reaches `exhausted_copy` (account-envelope 402 renders through the static billing family), so no billing branch exists. `nous_rate_limit` copy untouched (free-tier users genuinely have alternatives).

## Review trail

- Claude (3 rounds on the PR revisions, then a v4-delta check): **APPROVE** — "monotonically more conservative, no new false-suppression risk".
- GPT (independent paid-seat review): initial **CHANGES-NEEDED** (reason-alone gate could hide `/model` for sibling-model 429s) → both blockers resolved and confirmed: **APPROVE**.

## Contracts & verification

- Red on base before the fix (old copy emitted the clause with no viable alternative).
- New: generic-429 and short-reset contracts prove `/model` REMAINS; envelope+same-surface withholds; cross-surface/empty/malformed/deployment-scoped all keep; #89401 reset-window
title: fix(copy): advise /model on exhaustion only when a viable hop remains

author: dokterdok
body:
## What does this PR do?

**The problem.** Since #106742 merged, new cron runs are missing from their job's run history (#138812).
- **Desktop Cron page and sidebar:** every run fired after the switch shows as a dead row, with no click and no transcript. Older runs still open.
- **Runs API:** each new fire appears only as an output-file row.
- **Session detail:** no longer marks these sessions as cron-owned.

The runs themselves are fine; nothing can find them. An older bug is fixed along the way (#92133): job `backup`'s history also lists the runs of job `backup_weekly`.

**Why.** On the unified runtime a cron run gets a `local-<hash>` session id, but every history reader still looks for the old `cron_<job>_<timestamp>` id. The new id must stay: it is the hash of the fire's admission id, which exact-once retry depends on.

**The fix.** Runs are found through the record the runtime already keeps for every fire: the scheduler's admission, filed as `cron:<job>:<execution>`.
- **Lookup:** a new partial index makes this a range scan. In a synthetic benchmark it takes under 1 ms, where #138821's per-request scan took ~1.5 s at 40k sessions.
- **Legacy runs:** still found by id, but only when the id is the job prefix plus an exact timestamp. That fixes #92133.
- **Desktop:** decides that a row is a cron run from the row itself (`source: 'cron'`), not from the shape of its id.

**Proof.** On `main` the new tests fail: the `local-*` run is missing, detail ownership is `None`, and job `daily` lists the runs of `daily_digest`. The Desktop test fails too. All pass here. The first commit is #138821's (@KoNit-K), kept with its authorship.

**Before / after:**

| Surface | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SessionDB.list_cron_job_runs` / `GET /api/cron/jobs/{id}/runs` | post-switch runs missing; each shows up only as a synthetic `cron_output` doc row | listed as session rows, alongside legacy runs; output-doc and ledger rows are matched to their session by execution id, so a run appears once |
| Desktop Cron page and sidebar | new runs are inert rows (no click, no transcript) | open their transcript; a run is recognised by its row (`source: 'cron'`), with the legacy id as fallback |
| Session detail `scheduler_owned` | `None` for `local-*` runs (not recognised as cron) | works; ownership of a unified run is an exact execution match |
| Job `backup` vs job `backup_weekly` (legacy ids, #92133) | `backup`'s history also lists `backup_weekly`'s runs | a legacy id must
title: fix(cron): find unified-runtime cron runs by their scheduler admission

author: sharpnotebot
body:
## What does this PR do?

A background-process completion wake is refused with `admission_conflict` on every attempt, so it never reaches the session and is requeued unchanged (#138940 on Discord, #134889 on Telegram).

`snapshot_automation` restores the session's last committed native envelope and compared its source to the synthetic event's source exactly. The synthetic completion deliberately clears `source.message_id` (#52694, #123097) so a finished job does not reply-anchor to the message that started it, while Discord and Telegram put the human message id on the committed source. `SessionSource.to_dict()` writes `message_id` only when it is truthy, so the two sides could never be equal.

This PR compares the routing/provenance identity of both sources with only `message_id` excluded, keeps every other source field and the adapter identity check, and drops `message_id` from the persisted automation envelope so the wake cannot anchor to the stale human message (it restores as `message_id=None`). The key is omitted rather than stored as `null` because that is the canonical `SessionSource.to_dict()` format (it never writes a null anchor), so the stored source looks exactly like one built from a source with no `message_id`, and no new null key enters the hashed payload.

Fingerprint compatibility is supported only by a digest probe, not by an integration test: hashing a payload whose source omits `message_id` gives the same digest as one whose `message_id` was popped, and a different digest from one carrying `message_id: null`. Retrying, across versions, an admission recorded before this change is **not** tested here.

#138947 is complementary rather than a duplicate: it bounds the retry loop for a refused admission (stops the log flood), while this PR removes the cause of the refusal so the wake is actually delivered. Both can land.

- Telegram report and local patch: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6186546483
- Follow-up analysis: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6186798418

author: dokterdok
body:
## What does this PR do?

**The problem.** Desktop can refuse to use a profile that the local gateway is serving normally. This happens in two ways, both reproduced on `main` (`7bda2a33`):

1. **On macOS, Desktop hangs on its startup window** (#138754). By default a Mac disk ignores letter case, so a home path can be written as `/Users/Me/…` when the folder on disk is `/Users/me/…`, and both work. Every request then fails with `Noncanonical gateway profile`. Desktop retries, gets the same answer and never finishes starting. The reporter only got Desktop to start by correcting the case of their home path.
2. **Linked profiles don't work.** Some named profiles under `profiles/` are a symlink (macOS, Linux) or a junction (Windows), for example a profile kept on another drive. Desktop lists such a profile, but every request for it is refused.

**Why.** Desktop and the gateway name the same folder differently, and Desktop compares the names as text. The gateway uses Python's `Path.resolve()`, which follows links and keeps the letter case it was given. Desktop asks Node for the on-disk spelling and requires an exact match. It also builds `profiles/<name>` by joining text, without following the link the gateway followed.

**The fix.** Desktop now names a home exactly as the gateway does, and mints its tickets for that name.
- On macOS and Linux it uses a port of Python's `posixpath.realpath`.
- On Windows it uses Node's `realpath`, which already matches.

The safety check stays: a home that leads through a link to some other folder is still refused. The gateway's own checks are unchanged and still have the final say. A profile whose folder is gone now gets a clear `Profile '<name>' does not exist` instead of a raw `ENOENT` and a reconnect.

**Proof.**
- **macOS** (case-insensitive APFS): the case test fails on `main` with `Noncanonical gateway profile` and passes here.
- **Windows:** the junction test runs through the real runtime bridge and the gateway's ticket checks. It fails on `main` and passes here.
- **Parity:** a test checks Desktop's result against Python 3.14's own `Path.resolve()`.

**Before / after:**

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS, case-insensitive APFS, gateway home spelled in another letter case than on disk (#138754) | every ticket mint throws `Noncanonical gateway profile`. The error is stale, so Desktop re-ensures, gets the same path and stays on its startup window | the home is named the way the gateway names it, and the

author: dokterdok
body:
## What does this PR do?

**The problem.** Picking a model in a Desktop Bot Chat, or with `/model` in the CLI, TUI or ACP, can go wrong in three ways. All three are reproduced on `main` (`7bda2a33`):

1. **The pick fails and the chat is stuck on its model** (#138879). The picker answers `internal error`. The error comes from reading the credentials of the model the chat is *on*, so no pick can succeed.
2. **The new provider's key is sent to the old one.** Move a profile from provider A to provider B (new endpoint, new key). Its Bot Chat follows and runs on B. Now pick a model in that chat: Hermes checks the pick against A's endpoint with B's key, then moves the chat back to A.
3. **A replaced alias keeps sending its own key.** A chat started on a model alias that carries its own API key keeps sending that key after a profile change replaces the pick. It now goes to the profile's new endpoint instead of the profile's own key.

**Why.** The model switch builds "where the session is now" from two places. It takes the endpoint frozen when the session was created, and the key of the route the session runs today. Once a following session's profile moves, the two no longer match. Before #106742, Hermes took the whole route (provider, model, endpoint and key) from the live runtime at once.

**The fix.** The pick now switches from the route the session runs now, read once under one read of its profile. If that route cannot authenticate, the pick switches from its configured provider name alone, as the agent-less `--provider` path did before #106742, and the target resolves its own key. A launch key is sent only while the session is on the route it was bound to.

**Proof.** Three new tests fail on `main` and pass here, one per case above. The first case fails on `main` with the exact `AuthError` from #138879. Three control tests pass on both.

**Before / after:**

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session.mutate operation=model` (Desktop composer, Ink, ACP, classic CLI `/model`) on a following session (`follow_profile_config`, Bot Chat) after the profile moved to another endpoint | switches from the frozen **creation** endpoint (`old.provider` / `old.base_url`) with the **current** route's key, so endpoint validation sends the current key to the endpoint the profile left | switches from the route the session runs now: model, endpoint and key come from one resolution of the session's own route, under one read of the profile (main took them from the liv
title: fix(gateway): keep a local session's endpoint and key together on a model pick

## What does this PR do?

The gateway, not the client, now picks the coding toolsets for a session (`agent.coding_context: focus` in a code workspace → `coding` plus enabled MCP servers). Every interactive surface (CLI, TUI, Desktop, ACP, oneshot) gets the choice from one place.

- **A stored decision instead of a guess.** A session that follows the profile config re-derived "this session started in a code workspace" from `"coding" in self.toolsets`. A session created without `cwd` collapsed the same way. The policy now carries `coding_posture: bool`, set once at creation. `current_toolsets` replays it without re-probing the folder every turn.
- **One MCP-server list.** `coding_context._enabled_mcp_servers` now uses `enabled_mcp_server_names`. The CLI display, the legacy TUI factory and the gateway therefore list the same servers, plugin-provided ones included, and the gateway reuses the shared detection instead of re-implementing it.

author: Seldash
body:
## problem

`get_scratch_dir(prune=True)` is where idle-scratch retention is enforced: it sweeps at most once
per process, and across processes at most hourly (`.last_prune` stamp). Both triggers need a
process to *resolve* the scratch dir, so a host whose only long-lived process is the gateway never
re-sweeps after boot — entries that go idle later outlive the 24h idle window that
`SCRATCH_MAX_IDLE_HOURS` documents, until something outside Hermes clears them.

That is exactly the gateway's case: it is the process that is always up, and it already owns the
periodic chores (`_start_gateway_housekeeping`), where the media caches, the paste dir and the
checkpoint store all prune from the tick.

Measured on a long-running install: retention *does* hold whenever processes churn, since every new
process that resolves the scratch dir re-arms the hourly stamp. So this closes a gap in the
guarantee for churn-free hosts (`TMPDIR` points into `cache/scratch` for every Hermes child); it is
not a regression fix.

## fix

- `gateway/run.py`: new `_housekeeping_scratch_prune()` — a thin caller of
  `hermes_constants.prune_scratch_dir()` — registered in the housekeeping chore list at the 60-tick
  (hourly) cadence: the same cadence, and the same 24h max-idle rule, the platform media caches
  use. Registered after the per-tick chores for the same reason the checkpoint prune is: a sweep
  that actually deletes can hold the thread.
- `tests/gateway/test_scratch_prune_housekeeping.py`: new, 2 tests.

Cost stays bounded by the existing rule — only a tree already idle for the whole window pays for a
full walk, a live one stops at its first recent write (`subtree_touched_since`).

## tests

Red/green on base `7bda2a3368` (same worktree, `scripts/run_tests.sh`, per-file isolation):

```
BASE    gateway/run.py at origin/main, new test present   2 failed
PATCHED gateway/run.py + new test                         2 passed
```

New test file behaviour:

- `test_scratch_sweep_rides_the_hourly_tick` — 59 ticks → 0 sweeps, 60 → 1 (not every tick).
- `test_scratch_sweep_delegates_to_the_retention_helper` — the chore calls
  `prune_scratch_dir()` with no arguments; the rule stays in `hermes_constants`.

Regression — `tests/gateway/` + `tests/cron/` in the same worktree, patched vs the identical tree
with only this change reverted to `origin/main` (new test moved aside so both runs see the same
file set), comparing failure *sets* rather than counts, because this host has a large pre-existin

## What does this PR do?

On an always-on install (gateway + separately launched `hermes dashboard`, the normal setup for remote/phone access), every dashboard write action on a single session — delete, rename, pin, model, branch — fails with a bare 409. The dashboard process is not the store owner while a gateway serves the same home, so its offline mutation path can never win the `exclusive_maintenance` reservation; under `uvicorn log_level="warning"` the handled 4xx leaves no server-side trace, which is why this reads as a "UI bug".

This PR makes the standalone (no composed `session_authority`) mutation path hand the edit to the live owner first: discover the selected home's gateway endpoint (read-only, never starts a gateway), then forward the same revision-fenced `session.mutate` verb the gateway already exposes over the control socket. The owner's refusal verdicts map to the same HTTP statuses the offline path already uses (`permission_denied` → 403, `not_found` → 404, …; unmapped verdicts stay 409). With no discoverable owner — or one that dies between discovery and dial — the offline store path decides exactly as before, so genuinely owner-less homes are unchanged.

Fixes #138915

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

- `hermes_cli/web_server_sessions.py`: new `_mutate_via_gateway_owner(profile, params)` — read-only endpoint discovery for the selected home, then `connect_gateway(endpoint=...)` (the endpoint's own control socket, so a served `?profile=` reaches its owner) and one `session.mutate` RPC with the request's CAS tuple; dial failures return `None` so the caller falls back, owner refusals propagate.

- Network: sends the query text to the operator-configured sub-backends (registered search providers or operator-defined custom HTTP endpoints); the optional LLM re-rank calls the operator-configured ranker provider. No telemetry, no other network I/O.

author: grinco
body:
Adds a user-guide page next to the iron-proxy and network-isolation ones: how
to let Hermes work with mail, calendars or business systems without ever
giving it those credentials. A separate broker holds the keys, does the work as
another OS user, and hands back one bounded JSON result. New access and
writes get approved by a person on another device.

The page is upfront about the limits. The main one: cron, `-q` and other
unattended sessions never reach an approval transport (and `-z` runs in YOLO
mode), so it doesn't promise remote approval there.

One section uses Vornik as the example, the way the secrets page names
Bitwarden. I maintain Vornik, so happy to drop that section if you'd rather
keep the page vendor-free.

Built locally with `build:fast`: no new warnings, and all the links resolve.
title: docs(egress): running Hermes behind an external broker

author: zureyewz
body:
## Summary

Every config writer now runs inside a per-path transaction (`_config_transaction_lock`):
a thread `RLock` plus an OS file lock (`fcntl.flock` / `msvcrt.locking`, fork-safe via
`register_at_fork`, re-entrancy tracked per thread). On top of serialization:

- **Contended-writer merge**: when a full-document writer (`atomic_config_write` /
  `atomic_config_replace` / `atomic_roundtrip_config_write`) *waited* on the lock, keys
  that appeared on disk while it waited are merged in
  (`_preserve_unmentioned_config_keys`) instead of being overwritten by the stale
  snapshot the writer started from.
- **Rebasing RMW**: `atomic_config_update(path, mutator)` runs the mutator against the
  latest raw config under the lock, snapshots a baseline, and rebases the resulting
  delta over any non-cooperating writer that touched the file mid-mutator
  (`_rebase_config_mapping_delta`) — intentional deletions survive, unrelated
  concurrent keys survive.
- **Callers converted**: `auth._update_config_for_provider` and
  `auth._reset_config_provider` become `atomic_config_update` mutators;
  `agent_import.dump_yaml_file(..., baseline=...)` rebases agent-import `config.yaml`
  writes the same way.
- **`unset_config_value` legacy fix**: the RMW lambda now removes *both* the redirected
  key and the legacy `gateway.platforms.*` source, so a value living only under the
  legacy nested block is actually unset.

## Motivation (real incident)

A production race erased a concurrent writer's key: two writers read the same old YAML,
and the later full-document write clobbered the earlier writer's key. Upstream's
`atomic_config_write` already refuses *omitted* mapping keys, but refusal does not help
a writer whose snapshot went stale while it waited on a lock — and plain refusal would
discard that writer's own intended change.

## Changes

- `hermes_cli/config.py`: `_config_transaction_lock`, `_reset_config_locks_after_fork`,
  `_atomic_config_write_unlocked`, `atomic_config_update`,
  `_rebase_config_mapping_delta`, `_preserve_unmentioned_config_keys`,
  `atomic_roundtrip_config_write`, `atomic_roundtrip_config_update`; lock + contended
  merge wired into `atomic_config_write` / `atomic_config_replace`; `unset_config_value`
  dual-key unset inside the RMW.
- `hermes_cli/auth.py`: provider-switch and reset paths route through
  `atomic_config_update` mutators.
- `hermes_cli/agent_import.py`: `dump_yaml_file` gains an optional `baseline` and
  rebases `config.yaml` imports over
title: Config: per-path transaction lock; contended writers merge, RMWs rebase

author: zureyewz
body:
## Summary

Checkpoint stores are code/text snapshots, not media archives. This PR enforces that
invariant fail-closed at both boundaries:

- **Staging**: after `git add`, every staged raster path is dropped from the per-project
  index (`_drop_raster_from_index`), and a final verification scan
  (`_verify_no_raster_in_index`) runs immediately before `git write-tree`. Any raster
  path that survives either scan aborts the checkpoint (returns `False`) instead of
  committing it.
- **Restore**: single-file restores refuse raster paths outright; full-directory
  restores filter raster paths out of the restore plan (reported as
  `skipped_excluded_media`) and pass case-insensitive `icase,glob` pathspec excludes to
  `git checkout`, so generated media can never be resurrected from a checkpoint.
- **Store hygiene**: raster globs join `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` (with case-insensitive
  catch-alls), and a new `_ensure_default_excludes` (thread-lock guarded) merges the
  required patterns into *existing* stores' `info/exclude`, so pre-raster stores are
  upgraded and a custom `!*.png` negation cannot re-enable media. Custom non-raster
  patterns are preserved.

`_RASTER_SUFFIXES` (frozenset): `.png .jpg .jpeg .webp .gif .bmp .tif .tiff .avif
.heic .heif .ico`.

## Motivation (real incident)

A 3.6 GB `state.db` store got flooded by binary/image payloads being staged into
checkpoint git objects. Checkpoint capture and rollback slowed to a crawl and the
store bloated with content that rollback could never meaningfully restore. Excludes
alone were not enough: a store created before the excludes existed kept its tracked
raster, and custom negation rules could silently re-enable it — hence the verify +
fail-closed guards at both boundaries rather than a single filter.

## Changes

- `tools/checkpoint_manager.py`:
  - `_RASTER_SUFFIXES` constant; raster globs in `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES`.
  - `_ensure_default_excludes()` + `_EXCLUDE_REFRESH_LOCK`; called on new *and*
    existing stores in `_init_store`.
  - `_drop_raster_from_index()` (chunked `git rm --cached`, batches of 200, with a
    re-verify scan) and `_verify_no_raster_in_index()` (pre-write-tree boundary).
  - Restore-path guards: raster suffix check on `file_path`, plan filtering with
    `skipped_excluded_media` result reporting, and `icase` glob excludes on
    full-directory checkout.

## Test evidence

New/updated tests in `tests/tools/test_checkpoint_manager.py`:

- `test_file_count_guard_includes_raster_only_traversal`
title: Checkpoints: fail-closed raster-media guards at staging and restore boundaries

body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes how Hermes Desktop reaches a remote gateway a pluggable concern, by adding a `remote` plugin seam. Remote plugins register a supported scheme (i.e. `iroh://`) and own the routing transport. Hermes core (this PR's target) requires no new dependencies. A reference transport: [an iroh-based remote plugin](https://github.com/agentbox-tech/hermes-iroh-remote).

`CONTRIBUTING.md` § *Third-Party Product Integrations* prescribes this shape of PR:

> If your plugin needs a capability the framework doesn't expose, that's a feature request to **widen the generic plugin surface** (a new hook or `ctx` method) — never special-case your plugin in core.

Custom remote transports cannot exist today (Desktop speaks `https://` only). This PR follows the same shape as the ConfigBackend seam (#134369) and the kanban backend seam (#136097). My earlier spike (#137117) added iroh to Hermes, proving the transport but bundling a third-party product into core.

## Related Issue

No issue, I'm opening this draft as an RFC.

Related context: #70784 (iroh for A2A communication), #137117 (direct integration of the iroh transport into Hermes core).

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

**Server half** — scheme registry + plugin API + first-party CLI:

- `gateway/remote_plugins.py` (new) — `RemotePlugin` ABC (`serve()` / `connect()`) with `ServeHandle` / `RemoteTarget` (an **opaque** url Desktop fetches as-is); scheme validation (`^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*$`), built-in schemes rejected.
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py` — `PluginContext.register_remote_plugin` + module-level registration (mirrors `register_memory_provider`).
- `hermes_cli/subcommands/remote.py` (new) — `hermes remote {serve,connect,list,shutdown}`; a headless box can `hermes remote connect` with no desktop present, which is what makes the ABC bidirectional.
- `hermes_cli/main.py` — subcommand registration.
- `plugins/plugin_loader.py` — no-op context method alongside the other registration no-ops.

**Desktop half** — the scheme registry at the dial sites:

- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-plugin-registry.ts` (new) — `scheme → remote plugin` with `ensure(rawUrl)` as the single dial site; live dials keyed by the exact saved url, dial-once / teardown-once.
- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-plugin-dial.ts` (new) — `resolveRemoteBaseUrl()`: remote-plugin-backed urls dial first; plain https normalizes unchanged (core path untouched).

author: wenzetan
body:
## Problem

Discord's slash-command picker shows **English descriptions for every command that comes from `COMMAND_REGISTRY`**, even when `display.language` is a non-English locale whose catalog contains a translation for that command.

Measured on a live bot (71 registered application commands, `display.language: zh`):

- 29 commands localized — the ones in `_NATIVE_SLASH_COMMAND_SPECS`, which resolve through `t()`
- **42 commands still English** — `/agents`, `/busy`, `/goal`, `/context`, `/sessions`, `/memory`, `/rollback`, `/fast`, `/moa`, `/pause`, `/profile`, `/review`, … i.e. exactly the `COMMAND_REGISTRY` set that reaches the tree through `_auto_register()`
- Option/parameter descriptions *are* localized (they use the i18n template `platform.discord.command.auto_args_description`), so the picker ends up mixed: localized parameter text, English command text.

Telegram and Slack do not have this problem — both derive their menus through `hermes_cli/commands_platforms.py`, which already calls `cmd.describe()`.

## Root cause

`CommandDef.describe()` exists precisely for this and falls back to the English source when a catalog lacks the key:

```python
# hermes_cli/commands.py
def describe(self) -> str:
    """Localized description (``slash.<name>.description``); ``description`` is the English source."""
    return _localized(f"slash.{self.name}.description", self.description)
```

The Discord auto-register loop passed the raw field:

```python
# plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py (before)
for cmd_def in COMMAND_REGISTRY:
    if _is_gateway_available(cmd_def, config_overrides):
        _auto_register(cmd_def.name, cmd_def.description, cmd_def.args_hint)
        #                                      ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ English source, never localized
```

## Fix

One line:

```diff
             for cmd_def in COMMAND_REGISTRY:
                 if _is_gateway_available(cmd_def, config_overrides):
-                    _auto_register(cmd_def.name, cmd_def.description, cmd_def.args_hint)
+                    _auto_register(cmd_def.name, cmd_def.describe(), cmd_def.args_hint)
```

## Verification

Offline, same interpreter, `HERMES_LANGUAGE=zh`, enumerating exactly the gateway-available registry the Discord loop iterates:

```
gateway-available registry commands: 68
```

## Summary
Preserve exact dashboard respawn argv and account for restart follow-ups by component, rather than reporting every dashboard/serve failure as gateway debt.

Fixes #138903. Related: #136159. The exact-argv capture overlaps #136245 and #127204; the component-debt handling, PID-less reconciliation and handoff remedies address the additional attribution problem.

## Changes
### Exact process arguments
- Keep Linux's `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` capture and use psutil's exact argv before the `ps` fallback.
- Refuse Python `-c` commands reconstructed solely from lossy `ps` display text.
- Preserve exact inline source and spaced arguments; do not globally decode literal `012` or rewrite bootstrap source.

### Component-specific restart obligations
- Track gateway restart debt independently of dashboard cleanup failures.
- Record both `dashboard_restart` and `gateway_restart` when both components owe work; display both remedies in POSIX and PowerShell handoffs.
- Preserve genuine standing gateway obligations, but clear a false gateway marker when only dashboard work remains.
- Track unaccounted serve/dashboard rows separately from stopped PIDs. Retain dashboard follow-ups for PID-less rows and distinguish unverified old-code runtimes from stopped backends.
- Reuse the existing serve-kind classification. No authentication, profile ownership, configuration or session-data changes.

author: philoengineer
body:
## What does this PR do?

The Anthropic official-docs snapshot in `agent/usage_pricing.py` has no rows for `claude-haiku-5-5`, `claude-fable-5` or `claude-fable-5-1`. A direct Anthropic session on any of them misses the table and falls through to the cache-only models.dev lookup. With a cold `models_dev_cache.json`, or a `base_url` that isn't `anthropic.com`, the session records `cost_status="unknown"`, `cost_source="none"` and `$0` in `estimated_cost_usd`.

This adds them from [Anthropic's pricing page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing), using the existing shapes:

| Model | Input | Output | Cache read | 5m cache write |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `claude-fable-5` | $10.00 | $50.00 | $1.00 | $12.50 |
| `claude-fable-5-1` | $10.00 | $50.00 | **$0.25** (0.025× input, footnote 1) | $12.50 |
| `claude-haiku-5-5` ≤100K prompt | $0.10 | $0.50 | $0.01 | $0.125 |
| `claude-haiku-5-5` >100K prompt | $0.50 | $2.50 | $0.05 | $0.625 |

Haiku 5.5 is priced by prompt length. Anthropic counts every input token toward the threshold, cache reads and writes included, and prices the whole request at the higher rate. That is what the existing `tier_threshold_tokens` / `*_above` fields and `CanonicalUsage.prompt_tokens` already implement for Gemini Pro and GPT-6, so this is a new row only, with no new code.

## Related PRs

- #134546 covers `claude-sonnet-5-5` and the stale Sonnet 5 intro-price note, so both are left out here. Both PRs add an `anthropic-pricing-2026-10` group after the Opus 5 group. Whichever merges second has a trivial conflict: the rows from both PRs just go into one group.
- #43317 (closed by its author) and #45238 add the same `claude-fable-5` row.
- #101068 includes `claude-fable-5-1` at the same $0.25 but conflicts with the current table layout.
- #136380 generalizes context tiers (`pricing_tiers`). The Haiku 5.5 row uses the existing `tier_threshold_tokens` fields, which that PR keeps as the first overlay, so they should compose.
- Related: #134761 (Haiku 5.5 1M context) and #137890 (curated catalog entries).

Out of scope: Bedrock rows, 1h cache-write rates (#126415), and Haiku 5.5's new tokenizer vs. the chars/4 local estimate.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/usage_pricing.py`: new `anthropic-pricing-2026-10` snapshot group (Fable 5, Fable 5.1); tiered `claude-haiku-5-5` row next to the other context-tiered rows.
- `tests/agent/test_usage_pricing.py`: parame

author: timrichardson
body:
## What does this PR do?

On a PM-managed source install, `hermes --tui` could neither start a gateway nor recover one unless a gateway was already running: Ink's gateway bootstrap helper died with `No module named 'ruamel'` (#138878).

Ink runs `ui-tui/scripts/gateway_bootstrap.py` and `ui-tui/scripts/clipboard_image.py` on `HERMES_PYTHON` with `PYTHONPATH=<root>` only. On a source install `HERMES_PYTHON` is PM's store Python, which owns no packages, so the generation the launcher activated never reaches these children. With no owner running, discovery's fallback imports `ruamel` (`gateway.status` → `utils` → `hermes_yaml`), so both `--start` and `--recover` die. The clipboard helper loses Pillow, so non-PNG Wayland clipboard images silently depend on ImageMagick being installed.

Both helpers now call `pm.environments.activate_dependencies(root)` before anything imports a dependency.

**Why this approach:** it is the boot `hermes_bootstrap` runs for every other entry point, and the one `cron/worker_bootstrap.py` already uses for the same class of child. Restoring `PYTHONPATH` in `gatewayClient.ts`/`imageAttachments.ts` would not lease the committed generation or run its `.pth` files (the reasoning in `cron/worker_bootstrap.py`'s docstring). This approach also works however Ink was launched. On interpreters that own their packages (Nix, venvs) it is a no-op. The parent launcher has already run the rest of `hermes_bootstrap` (source-update completion, relaunch), so these short-lived helpers need only the dependency boot.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138878

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope go to [Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) first, not a public PR)

- `ui-tui/scripts/clipboard_image.py`: same, before saving the clipboard image (sibling path, same cause).

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

`session.mutate`'s `model` operation resolves the session's **current** runtime before applying a switch, only to feed the switch's probe credential (`current_api_key`) and the route-change comparison. When the session's frozen policy carries a bare `custom` provider placeholder that cannot re-resolve (the shape reported in #138879: the session row's `model_config.gateway_runtime.provider` is `"custom"` while the profile declares `custom:deepseek`), `_resolve_session_agent_runtime` walks the frozen fallback chain, ends on the credentialless default endpoint, and `_raise_for_credentialless_bare_custom` raises `AuthError` out of that lookup. The whole RPC then crashes with "internal error" **before the requested target model is ever looked at** — every model switch on such a session fails, exactly the one action that would replace the dead route.

This PR degrades that pre-switch lookup to an empty runtime on `AuthError` and lets the switch proceed. The target resolves its own credentials from config (`user_providers` / `custom_providers` are passed to `switch_model` from the policy's config regardless), and the remaining uses of `runtime` (`selection_warnings`' probe key, `selection_route_changed`'s base_url) already treat it as optional with `or ''` fallbacks. This mirrors the older TUI path (`tui_gateway.model_switch._apply_model_switch`), which snapshots the live agent instead of re-resolving the frozen policy and therefore never hits this crash.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138879

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session_mutation_model.py`: wrap the pre-switch `_resolve_session_agent_runtime` lookup in `try/except AuthError`; on failure log a warning and continue with `runtime = {}` so the mutation proceeds on the target's own config-resolved credentials.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/gateway/test_session_mutation_model.py -q` — 6 passed, 1 skipped (linux-only e2e) on macOS 25.4, including the new regression test `test_unresolvable_pre_switch_route_does_not_kill_the_switch`.
2. The new test builds a policy whose runner raises the exact `AuthError("provider 'custom' resolved without credentials")` from the issue's traceback and asserts `prepare_model` still commits the switch (`switched.model == 'b'`); without the fix it raises instead.
3. Observed result: the mutation completes and the committed policy carries the target model, so the dead `custom` route
title: fix(gateway): switch models away from an unresolvable frozen route

author: ranggaoscar
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a notification-poller leak when an agent is rebuilt for an existing TUI session, such as during an in-session `/model` switch, resume, or late MCP refresh.

**Root cause:** `_start_session_services` replaced `rec["_notif_stop"]` without setting the previous stop event. Each rebuild could leave another daemon poller running for the same session. Those loops continued consuming the process-global completion queue and handling loop, heartbeat, and bot-mailbox notifications, while session finalization could signal only the newest event.

**Patch:** Set the previous stop event under `_sessions_lock` before starting and recording its replacement. The old loop exits through its existing stop-event/finalization checks; it is not joined while holding the lock. One active poller remains after the old loop exits. The existing shared notification-deduplication state is retained.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138806

author: xingzihai
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes a `RecursionError` in the Codex Responses API preflight: `_neutralize_harmony_structure()` recursed into every list/tuple element and dict value with no depth budget. A deeply nested outbound payload (e.g. a `tools[].parameters` schema from an external/MCP tool, or a replayed reasoning `summary`) of ~496+ levels exhausted the interpreter frame budget and crashed the whole API call during preflight (unhandled `RecursionError`).

The fix adds a depth budget (`_HARMONY_STRUCTURE_MAX_DEPTH = 512`): below the cap behavior is byte-identical; above it, values are copied without further descent, so a ~6 KB payload is a copy instead of a crash. Reserved-token detection in object keys still runs at every level, so the existing `ValueError` contract is unchanged.

author: KoNit-K
body:
## What does this PR do?

This allows an administrator's managed scope to impose a one-way outbound telemetry ceiling. Before this change, `resolve_send_config` considered only the active profile, so a profile with `telemetry.shared_metrics.enabled: true` and `send: true` could upload metrics even when the managed configuration declared `send: false`. The resolver now reads that managed value only as a prohibition: managed `false` disables transmission while managed `true` cannot create profile consent.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138804

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/observability/shared_metrics_send_config.py` — reads the managed shared-metrics policy and applies an explicit `send: false` as an outbound-only ceiling.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_shared_metrics_send_config.py` — proves the ceiling blocks an opted-in profile and that managed `send: true` leaves an opted-out profile unsent.

## How to Test

- [x] `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_shared_metrics_send_config.py` — 21 passed.
- [x] `ruff check hermes_cli/observability/shared_metrics_send_config.py tests/hermes_cli/test_shared_metrics_send_config.py` — passed.
- [x] CONTROL: the focused suite retains the existing collection-required and endpoint-safety cases, including an unrequested send remaining off.

## Evidence

- BEFORE RED: with a managed `telemetry.shared_metrics.send: false` mapping and a profile requesting send, the focused assertion received `SendConfig(..., send=True)`.
- AFTER GREEN: the same focused suite reports 21 passed; managed `false` returns `send=False` while local collection remains enabled.
- CONTROL: managed `send: true` does not turn on a profile whose own `send` setting is false, and the existing safe-endpoint cases remain green.

author: strnadchristopher
body:
## What does this PR do?

Linux has no native window material, so **Translucency** only works on macOS and Windows. Compositors like Hyprland, KWin and picom can blur what's behind an alpha-capable window, but Electron only honors alpha when a window is *created* `transparent`. Right now that means no theme or plugin can paint a see-through background on Linux.

This PR adds a Linux-only opt-in: `HERMES_DESKTOP_TRANSPARENT=1`.

- Chat windows are created with `transparent: true` and a clear backing.
- Live translucency and theme re-applies keep that backing clear instead of switching back to the opaque theme color.
- Built-in themes still paint an opaque page, so nothing looks different until a theme's `customCSS` asks for transparency. Window `opacity` is never used, so text and images stay solid.
- It's off by default and does nothing on macOS or Windows.

To keep `main.ts` from growing (code-health gate), `chatWindowSurfaceOptions` moves into `electron/translucency.ts` with its comments unchanged and takes its platform inputs as arguments. The runtime backing choice moves next to it as `windowBackingColor`. Net effect: `main.ts` is 30 lines shorter.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking, opt-in)
- [x] Documentation (`website/docs/user-guide/desktop.md`, new "Transparent windows on Linux" section)

## How to test

```bash
cd apps/desktop && npx vitest run electron/translucency.test.ts
HERMES_DESKTOP_TRANSPARENT=1 hermes desktop   # on a compositor with blur, with a theme that sets a translucent background
```

## Verification

- `electron/translucency.test.ts`: **78 passed**, including 4 new tests. They cover: env gating (Linux + exactly `1`), opted-in windows created transparent with no `opacity`, unchanged options for windows that don't opt in, and the runtime backing staying clear.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit`: clean
- `python scripts/check`: **12 checks, ok**. Code health reports 0 blocking. The first version added lines to `main.ts` and failed this gate, which is why the extraction is part of this PR.
- Live check on Hyprland, using a throwaway instance on a headless output with otherwise identical launches:
  - `HERMES_DESKTOP_TRANSPARENT=1` → the renderer surface captures as **RGBA**
  - unset → **RGB** (opaque)
- Visual check on Hyprland with blur: the wallpaper shows through, blurred, while text stays crisp.

## Checklist

- [x] Opt-in, off by default, Linux-only
- [x] Tests added
- [x] Docs updated
- [ ] Not tested
title: feat(desktop): opt-in transparent chat windows on Linux

## What does this PR do?

`hermes memory setup`'s generic schema walker (`hermes_cli/memory_setup.py::_prompt_schema_fields`, the non-secret/non-choice branch) called `_prompt(desc, default=str(effective_default))` and stored whatever text came back. Accepting a list/dict default therefore persisted its Python repr:

```yaml
memory:
  mnemosyne:
    sync_roles: "['user']"
    reflect: "{'disabled_for_cron': True, 'max_calls_per_session': 3}"
```

Mnemosyne parses `sync_roles` as CSV, intersects `{"['user']"}` with its role names, gets an empty set, and stops automatic conversation capture — while `hermes memory status` still reports the provider healthy.

The fix maps the prompt answer back to the field's type:
- accepting the offered default keeps the native value (list, dict, bool, number);
- list/dict defaults are displayed as JSON, and an **edited** answer must parse (YAML/JSON, so `[user]` also works) to the same shape — otherwise the wizard prints `Ignoring <key>: expected a list such as ["user"]` and keeps the existing value instead of saving garbage;
- a saved empty list / `False` / `0` is no longer replaced by the schema default on re-run (`provider_config.get(key) or default` → only `None`/`""` fall back), so an intentional `sync_roles: []` survives, as the issue asks.

author: MohitBallikar
body:
## Problem

When the Hermes desktop app closes, the Electron main process kills the Python backend with SIGTERM. Python's `atexit` handlers do not fire on SIGTERM, so the existing cleanup hook in `_stop_at_exit()` is bypassed. The llama-server process tree (router + inference children) is orphaned, holding 20+ GB of RAM until the next Hermes boot cleans it up.

## Root Cause

`hermes_cli/local_runtime/bootstrap.py` only registered `atexit.register(shutdown_local_runtime)`. The desktop app's SIGTERM bypasses `atexit` entirely.

## Fix

Added SIGTERM/SIGINT signal handlers alongside the existing `atexit` hook:

```python
def _sigterm_handler(signum, frame):
    shutdown_local_runtime()
    signal.signal(signum, signal.SIG_DFL)
    os.kill(os.getpid(), signum)
```

- Calls `shutdown_local_runtime()` which terminates the full process tree via `LlamaServerSupervisor._terminate_tree()`
- Re-raises with `SIG_DFL` so the process still terminates after cleanup
- Guarded with `suppress(ValueError)` for non-main-thread contexts
- Idempotent via the existing `_EXIT_HOOKED` flag

## Cross-Platform Safety

| Platform | SIGTERM | SIGINT | Notes |
|----------|---------|--------|-------|
| Linux | ✅ | ✅ | Standard POSIX |
| macOS | ✅ | ✅ | Standard POSIX |
| Windows | ✅ | ✅ | Python 3.9+ maps to `TerminateProcess` |

## Test Coverage

Added `test_sigterm_handler_calls_shutdown`: spawns a subprocess that registers the SIGTERM handler and verifies `shutdown_local_runtime` is called before the process terminates.

## Review

Verified by parallel agent on `nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free` — confirmed correctness, cross-platform safety, and low regression risk.
title: fix(llamacpp): terminate server tree on SIGTERM/SIGINT so desktop close releases RAM

author: unsupportedpastels
body:
## What does this PR do?

On a Mac without Apple's Command Line Tools (CLT), the installer once again installs git for the user and carries on, instead of failing at the clone with a cryptic error. This restores the macOS git behavior the old installer had before the pm bootstrap rewrite.

### The problem

Fresh Macs fail the install with this error (reported from a live workshop, where several attendees hit it):

```
git clone failed; no checkout published: ... see man xcode-select
```

macOS ships `/usr/bin/git` as a stub until the CLT are installed. The stub is on `PATH`, but every call fails with `xcrun: error: invalid active developer path ... see man xcode-select`. The current `stage_prerequisites` only checks `command -v git`, which the stub passes, so the installer prints `prerequisites ok (git, curl)` and then dies at the first real git call, the clone. The message never mentions the Command Line Tools or what to run.

### How it worked before, and what changed

The pre-pm installer handled this case. `check_git` ran `git --version`, with the comment *"On fresh macOS /usr/bin/git is a stub that exits non-zero until CLT is installed."* If git failed, `attempt_install_git` installed it:

1. With Homebrew present, it ran `brew install git`, which needs no dialog.
2. Otherwise it ran `xcode-select --install` to open Apple's dialog. It then checked every 5 seconds, for up to 15 minutes, whether git worked, and continued the install in the same run.
3. If git still didn't work, it printed manual instructions and exited.

That code arrived with #20059 and was removed in 3d12e86ef1 (`feat(pm): unified package manager — pm store foundation`, part of #102765). That commit replaced the 3,600-line `install.sh` with a thin staged bootstrapper. Its stated scope was handing heavy dependencies (tool binaries, browsers, Node) to pm. pm deliberately leaves git to the system on macOS and Linux (`pm/packages.py`: *"POSIX uses the system git - a deliberate gap, not an oversight"*). The new bootstrapper kept only `command -v git || fail`.

The removal looks unintentional rather than a decision:

- Neither the commit message, the #102765 description, nor its review comments mention git auto-install, the macOS stub, Xcode, or the Command Line Tools. The PR describes the new scripts as thin bootstraps that "check the hashes of the pinned uv and Git from `pm/lock.json`, clone the repository, and hand off to PM". Pinned Git applies only to Windows.
- No test ever covered th
title: fix(install): install git on macOS again when /usr/bin/git is the CLT stub

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

A local `session.create` with an explicit `provider` but no `base_url` folded the provider into the frozen `model` block one key at a time, leaving the profile's existing `model.base_url` in place. The frozen route then paired the new provider with the previous provider's endpoint, so the runtime assembled `URL = old provider's host` with `credential = new provider's key`: the new provider's API key was sent to the old vendor's host (401 from the wrong vendor), and the failed call marked the pooled credential exhausted, hiding the real cause behind "main provider unavailable".

This makes a provider-only launch pick a whole-route change in `gateway/session_policy.py` → `_apply_launch_overrides()`: when the pick names a different provider than the profile's `model` block and the caller did not pass a `base_url`, the inherited route keys that belong to the replaced provider (`base_url`, `api_mode`, `key_env`, `api_key_env`, inline `api_key`/`api`, `api_key_from`) are dropped so the target provider resolves its own endpoint and credentials. This mirrors what a committed `/model` switch already rewrites (`model_selection_config_updates`). A caller that passes `base_url` explicitly keeps the route it built, and a same-provider re-pick keeps the profile's pins.

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do? Deleting a session that belongs to a non-root profile always failed with HTTP 409 `runtime_coordination_required` on a multiplexed gateway (the default topology: one process launched with the root HERMES_HOME owns every local session, Desktop primary connection on a sub-profile). A root-profile session deleted fine in the same window, so profile sessions looked undeletable from every Desktop client. Root cause: the delete `live_guard` in `write_mutation()` refused the mutation unless `store._routing_db.db_path == authority.db.db_path`. But since #66887 the routing index is pinned to the **launch home** for every profile (one flat index across all profiles), while `authority.db` is the store of the profile named in the request (`profiles/

/state.db`). For every secondary profile the two paths differ by construction, so the guard could never pass — it has been broken for multiplexed deletes since the day it landed. The guard's real question is "does one runtime coordinate both writes of this delete?" — the receipt commit into the profile store and the routing retire through the launch-home index. Every authority reaching `mutate_session` is resolved from the serving runner's own registry (`_session_mutation_context` → `authority_for_home`), and that same runner's store owns the routing index, so the two writes are always coordinated by one process. The guard now asks exactly that: `_runtime_owns_authority()` checks the authority belongs to its runner (`session_authorities` registry membership, falling back to the single `session_authority` for registry-less runners). An authority the runner does **not** hold still refuses with `runtime_coordination_required` (fail-closed preserved), and `store._routing_db is None` still refuses. ## Related Issue Fixes #138826 ## Type of Change - [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue) ## Changes Made - `gateway/session_mutations.py`: replaced the raw `db_path` equality in the delete `live_guard` with `_runtime_owns_authority(authority)` — a same-owner check (runner registry membership); kept the `_routing_db is None` refusal unchanged. - `tests/gateway/test_delete_secondary_profile_multiplex.py` (new): full multiplex runner (launch + `alpha` secondary) via the existing `_reserve_homes`/`_runner` fixtures; asserts the secondary's delete no longer 409s and actually removes both the profile-store row and the routing entry. Also covers `_runtime_owns_authority` fail-closed case
title: fix(gateway): let a multiplexed profile's delete pass the routing guard

## What does this PR do?

When `patch` falls back to the whitespace-normalized strategy, the match span can start inside the run of spaces before the match, so the edit deletes `run_len - 1` whitespace characters outside `old_string`. `_map_normalized_positions` (`tools/fuzzy_match.py:129`) tests `original[i] == normalized[j]` before the collapsed-whitespace branch, so the first space of a run advances the normalized index and the rest of the run is pinned to the next character. author: jackie-wayland
body:
## What does this PR do?

Makes a local (gateway-owned) session survive a frozen config secret that the profile has since stopped defining. Today that condition wedges **every read** of the chat with `launch_credentials_unavailable`, not just the credential it names.

A local session freezes the config secrets it launched with as a `profile-config-v1:` reference in `state.db` → `state_meta` → `gateway.local_policy.v1:<session>`: a list of config paths plus a value fingerprint per path. Every turn re-reads **only `config.yaml`**, so dropping a path from the profile — moving an env-routed key such as `API_SERVER_KEY` to `.env`, which is exactly what the settings flow does — leaves the reference permanently unverifiable. `recover_config_secrets` treated that the same as a rotated value, so it refused, and because the same recovery ran in read-only paths:

- turns died in `gateway/run_turn.py::_run_agent_display_settings` **before the agent started**;
- the Desktop model menu and reasoning picker failed with `JsonRpcGatewayError: launch_credentials_unavailable`, surfaced to the user as `模型选项更新失败` / “Model option update failed” — a *settings* error for a credential problem;
- and no restart repaired it (verified across three restarts: gateway + Desktop), with no CLI/RPC to re-freeze the policy or drop the entry.

Reported as the `CFG-1` finding.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (finding **CFG-1**: “Changing or removing **any** secret in `config.yaml` … makes every older local session unusable”). That tracker asks for new reports as comments rather than new issues, so this PR references it instead of “Fixes”.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session_policy_credentials.py` — separate *absent* from *changed*: an entry whose path is a **single top-level key** the profile no longer defines is skipped with a warning (the frozen tree keeps what it held); every **nested** path (`model.api_key`, `providers.*.api_key`, `mcp_servers.*.env`) still refuses, since those can carry the session's own route credential. A rotated value still refuses everywhere. (`_defined()` helper + one branch.)
- `gateway/run_turn.py` — `_run_agent_display_settings` reads the policy with `secrets=False`. Display, progress, status and toolset resolution consume settings only; the agent's own runtime still resolves the secrets, and still refuses there. ## Summary

Related to #138836. This is a bounded delivery-policy fix, not a complete fix for that issue's lifecycle/recovery requirements.

The Desktop/TUI Kanban poller previously claimed subscriptions by platform and exact session key, then woke the model for every formatted event. It ignored saved passive/wake mode, stamped notifier ownership and unsupported thread anchors.

- `notify` emits a passive status only; it does not buffer or start a model turn.
- `notify+wake` retains status delivery plus the existing idle-turn buffer.
- `wake` requests the turn without a passive status.
- Stamped notifier profiles are filtered before event claims, including when the read-only probe fails.
- Non-empty local thread anchors remain unclaimed instead of being delivered to a root session.
- Unstamped legacy rows retain exact-session/root compatibility, and diagnostic classification is preserved.
- Local delivery semantics and outstanding limitations are documented.

No new dependency, schema, configuration setting, tool, watcher or dispatcher is introduced.

author: benbarclay
body:
## Summary

On a gateway that reaches a platform only through the Relay, several delivery paths broke with the unified gateway runtime ([#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742)):

- **Messages waiting in the queue at a restart are never run.** A relay message that was committed and acknowledged, but hadn't started, stays `queued` after the gateway restarts. The connector already got its ACK, so it never redelivers either. This affects single-profile and multiplexed gateways.
- **Replies to restored sessions go out without the connector's routing fields.** The Relay's per-chat egress caches only fill on live inbound. A reply to a recovered turn, or to a heartbeat after a restart, therefore carried no `scope_id`/`user_id` for the connector to resolve a tenant from.
- **Discord component presses forwarded by the connector are refused.** A non-command `passthrough_forward` (MESSAGE_COMPONENT) failed native admission with `permission_denied` and never ran.

**Stacked on [#138742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/138742)** (connector-stamped profile admission), whose single-profile stamp handling this reuses. Merge #138742 first. The commits to review here are the last three.

This salvages [#131090](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/131090) by @jonpol01 (cherry-picked with authorship preserved). That PR was written before #106742 and fixed the adapter-selection half for the legacy revival paths. The rest is new, for the shared session-authority paths.

## Background for reviewers

A relayed source keeps its *logical* platform (`discord`). Relay provenance lives in the wire-invisible `delivered_via_upstream_relay` flag, which is never persisted. The Relay adapter is registered under `Platform.RELAY`. So any source rebuilt from durable state (a session origin) lacks the flag, and a lookup by its logical platform finds no adapter.

Under #106742, startup recovery (`recover_gateway_native_sessions`) binds each session that has queued admissions to `runner._adapter_for_source(entry.origin)`. For a relay-only platform that returned `None`, and `check_native_route` refused the binding as `not_found`.

In multiplex mode a second gap made this worse. A natively admitted session never persisted `SessionEntry.transport_profile`, because the routing entry is written from the source rebuilt out of the admission envelope, which carries no `RoutingIdentity`. So revival paths couldn't tell which bot received the lane.
title: fix(relay): run queued relay admissions after a restart, warm restored egress, admit forwarded components

author: mordekai-lab
body:
## What does this PR do?

Serialize cooperative `ui_meta` compare-and-swap updates across gateway/helper processes. The canonical helper in `hermes_cli/profiles_ui_meta.py` holds a stable per-profile advisory sidecar lock across the uncached read, revision check, key merge and atomic YAML replacement. The existing gateway configure handler delegates directly to it; the profiles facade is unchanged.

- Preserve key-wise merge, `None` deletion, persistent deletion revisions, all-or-nothing conflicts, existing wire keys and the historical JSON serialized-string size limit.
- Attribute accepted title writes/removals using that call's accepted value and revision, without reconstructing a previous title outside the transaction. Concurrent log ordering is not a linearizable audit trail.
- Refuse mutation when advisory locking is unavailable or acquisition fails. POSIX uses `flock`; the Windows branch initializes storage and seeks byte zero for acquisition and release. The sidecar is deliberately never unlinked.

This is cooperative metadata serialization, **not global profile transactionality**: unrelated whole-profile writers do not participate, and advisory-lock semantics on network filesystems are not guaranteed. Unconditional updates retain their existing lost-update risks. The lock acquisition deadline does not bound time spent waiting for the process-wide thread lock.

**Inherited permissive YAML behavior is unchanged.** Unreadable, malformed or nonmapping existing YAML is treated as an empty document by the existing reader; an accepted update can overwrite it. This does not implement strict reads. Lock-acquisition failures refuse the update, but errors after replacement, including unlock/logging errors, are not rollback guarantees.

No new RPC, schema, tool, dependency, facade re-export or code-health exemption is introduced.

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

The browser inactivity janitor (`_cleanup_inactive_browser_sessions`) built its stale-task list under `_cleanup_lock`, released the lock, and never looked again before tearing each session down. A browser command calling `_update_session_activity` in that window still had its session closed underneath it, so the next command failed or started a fresh browser.

This adds a recheck under the lock right before each teardown: re-read the session's last-activity timestamp and skip it when it is no longer past `BROWSER_SESSION_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT` (or its tracking vanished). The timestamp is taken *before* the read, so together with the lock a touch that completed before the recheck began is always seen. This is the minimal fix for the reported window; the wider "reserve the session so a racing command opens a fresh one" hardening from the issue would need the teardown path to stop re-resolving sessions by task id, which is a separate change.

author: RenegadeRocks
body:
## Summary
Fixes #138816. Two related problems with pinned cron jobs and provider throttling:

### 1. A pool-bench 429 read as a missing credential (blocked the job)
A job pinned to `claude-sonnet-5-5` failed pre-dispatch:
```
[blocked_config] provider credential missing: Anthropic credentials are rate-limited for
claude-sonnet-5-5; other Claude models remain available (see `hermes auth list`). …
Set the provider API key in .env (or `hermes setup`) …
```
The key was present and working for every other Claude model; the pool had benched it for one model after a 429. `is_rate_limited_auth_error` only recognised `CODEX_RATE_LIMITED_CODE`, while the native-Anthropic bench reports the condition in message text, so `_preflight_check_provider_key` took the missing-credential branch instead of letting `cron/quota_hold.py` hold the job.

- `is_rate_limited_auth_error` also matches the pool-bench wording.
- `_anthropic_token_or_raise` attaches `provider`, `retryable=True` and the pool's remaining cooldown as `retry_after`, so quota-hold can park the run until the window reopens.
- `CredentialPoolModelCooldownMixin.token_cooldown_seconds()` exposes that bench.

### 2. A pinned job could not fall back at all
`_job_fallback_chain` passed `declared=None` with `pinned=True`, so a pinned job had no chain — one throttled provider meant a failed run even with `fallback_providers` configured. It now resolves three layers, most specific first: the job's own `fallback_providers`, `cron.fallback_providers` (fleet-wide, for pinned jobs), then the global chain (unpinned jobs only). An explicit `[]` still disables fallback.

This lets an operator keep a cheap model on token-light jobs and still have them walk the same chain as everything else.

## Verification
- `is_rate_limited_auth_error`: True for the pool-bench error; False for a missing credential, a `relogin_required` error, a non-`AuthError`, and an entitlement 400. Codex's code path unchanged.
- Preflight probes stop blocking the two jobs that were failing (one satellite profile, one pinned to a non-Anthropic model), and all 12 pinned jobs across four profiles resolve a 3-entry chain.
- `retry_after` resolved to the live cooldown (~77 min) and `quota_hold.hold_seconds_from_failure` reads it.
- New tests: `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_pool_rate_limit.py` (8) and `tests/cron/test_job_fallback_chain.py` (5), 13 passed.
title: fix: pool-bench 429 is not a missing credential; let pinned cron jobs carry a fallback chain

author: teknium1
body:
A local terminal session whose working directory was deleted now runs the next command in the nearest usable parent and tells the model it moved, instead of failing every call with exit 126 until the gateway restarts.

Ported from lobehub/lobehub#20735 (their `local-file-shell` hit the same wedge: a pinned cwd that no longer exists failed every `runCommand` forever). Builds on @suhas-svg's #131554, whose diagnosis (recovery runs after the wrapper script already embedded the dead `cd`) is the core of this fix; their commit is kept with authorship.

## What changes

- `BaseEnvironment.execute()` resolves the effective cwd through a new `_usable_cwd()` hook **before** building the wrapper. `LocalEnvironment` swaps a missing/unenterable directory for `_resolve_safe_cwd()`'s pick (the existing #17558 / #66306 nearest-usable-ancestor rule). Docker/SSH/Modal etc. are untouched (identity hook).
- This covers the explicit `cwd=` the terminal tool passes from the session's recorded cd state. That is the path none of the open PRs reached: `_recover_cwd()` only repaired `self.cwd`, and only inside `_run_bash()`.
- The move is reported once as a `cwd_fallback` field on the tool result ("Working directory X no longer exists…; this command ran in Y instead, so relative paths resolved there…"). Background spawns (`spawn_local` already resolved a dead cwd silently) report it the same way.
- The session record heals from the next observed `pwd`, so the notice fires once.
- #131554's `file_operations.py` hunk is reverted: the execute-level resolution makes it redundant.

## Validation

| | `origin/main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Live `hermes chat -q` (Nous, claude-haiku-5.5; `pwd` → `rmdir <cwd>` → `ls -a .`), step 3 tool row read from the run's `state.db` | `cd: …/proj/sub: No such file or directory`, **exit 126**, hint "chmod +x it" | exit 0, ran in `…/proj`, `cwd_fallback` notice present |
| In-process real `terminal_tool` with the dir deleted externally, 2 calls | 126, 126 | 0 + notice, then 0 with no notice |
| `tests/tools/test_local_env_cwd_recovery_executes.py` (2 invariants, real bash) | 2 failed | 2 passed |
| 80 related files (`test_local*`, `test_terminal*`, `test_file_operations*`, `*cwd*`, `process_registry*`, `*background*`, `environments/`, `file_tools*`) | — | 912 passed, 0 failed |

I also ran the same in-process repro against the heads of the open sibling PRs #136153, #131554, #107163 and #137946. All four still exit 126 when both the session record
title: fix(terminal): a deleted working directory no longer wedges every command; the model is told where it ran (port lobehub#20735, salvage #131554)

body:
## Summary

Redesign the desktop Capabilities page (Skills, Plugins, Connectors, Tools) around a card-catalog surface, using Hermes theme tokens so it follows every theme in light and dark.

### Catalog redesign (desktop)

- Skills and Plugins browse through a native card catalog: bento shelves that work out their tile mix before placing anything — 2×2 showcases (entries with art only), two-wide cards and single cards, with `w = 4R − 3s − k` so every row fills edge to edge; no holes, no full-width filler. Categories with fewer than 3 entries share a "More to explore" shelf; plugins with an unlisted category file under General.
- Tools uses a feature row (Essentials before real usage data exists), themed two-column lists, and a toolset's settings in a dialog instead of a side panel.
- Connectors keeps its directory rows and drops the duplicate title; groups use the shared section heading.
- All four tabs share one content column, one centred scroller and one search field (`CapabilitySearch`: boxed, the tab's name as scope badge, the tab's actions at the end, data-derived "Try …" hints on Skills and Tools). Shared rhythm tokens set the gaps on every tab. Filter segments size to their labels (`SegmentedControl sizing="content"`).
- Cards have no border at rest and keep their per-card accent gradient, softened. On hover an arc fades in and sweeps the edge; every card runs the sweep on the document timeline, so moving to the next card carries it on instead of restarting. Hover paints instantly everywhere; only the exit eases. DESIGN.md's Motion section states the rule.
- Official entries get first-party artwork with a theme tint. Catalog data, install state, filters, detail dialogs and plugin/skill management stay on the existing feeds and stores.

### Featured picks, shared by the site and the app

- `apps/shared/src/catalog-curation.json` holds an ordered `featured` list per kind next to the artwork; changing the pick is a one-line edit.
- `extract-skills.py` / `extract-plugins.py` stamp a 1-based `featured` rank into `skills.json` / `plugins.json`, the files both the site and the app read.
- `pickFeatured` in `apps/shared` rotates through the ranks weekly so both surfaces show the same entry; falls back to newest official entry with art, then most-starred official entry with art. Never reads download counts.
- `/skills` and `/plugins` get a matching hero card (author, title, description, tags, action bottom-right, accent wash), shown while browsing everythin

## What does this PR do?

Moves the coding-posture toolset choice from the client into the gateway, so every interactive surface gets it from one place.

With `agent.coding_context: focus`, Hermes swaps the profile's default toolsets for the `coding` toolset (plus enabled MCP servers) when the session's folder is a code workspace (`agent/coding_context.py`). Until now that choice was made on the client:

body:
## What does this PR do?

`sessions delete` removes a session's durable row, but the authority's live registry keeps the routing entry for it. Nothing evicts that entry, and `authorize` only refuses an id absent from `self.sessions` entirely — so a live entry whose row is gone still passes authorization. `SessionAuthority._handle` then read `row['runtime_revision']` from a row that no longer exists and raised `TypeError`.

Both live feeders — `session.list` (`gateway/session_controls.py`) and `session.active_list` (`gateway/session_active_list.py`) — skip `RuntimeStoreError` reasons `{permission_denied, profile_mismatch, not_found}` and re-raise everything else, so a `TypeError` is fatal: one stale entry failed every listing until the gateway restarted. On the TUI gateway that is the whole session picker, exactly as reported.

The change refuses the missing row with the same `not_found` reason `authorize` already uses for an absent id, at the single point both feeders funnel through (`resolve` → `_handle`). `_reserve_route` creates the row at registration time, so a live entry with no row means genuinely gone; the entry is then skipped like any other gone session and the remaining rows still list.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138794
Fixes #138943

Both are the same signature: a live routing entry whose durable row is gone makes `session_authority._handle` raise `TypeError`, and every `session.list` fails until the gateway restarts. #138794 is the Windows/Ink report, #138943 the Docker/TUI one.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/session_authority.py`: `_handle` raises `RuntimeStoreError('not_found')` when the durable row is gone instead of indexing it.
- `tests/gateway/test_session_list_stale_entry.py`: regression test — a live entry whose row was deleted is skipped by `session.list` instead of failing it, and `resolve` reports `not_found` for it.

## How to Test

1. `uv run --group dev python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_session_list_stale_entry.py -q` — with the guard reverted this fails with `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable` at `gateway/session_authority.py:204`; it passes with the fix.
2. Regression over the family: `uv run --group dev python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_session_list_stale_entry.py tests/gateway/test_authority_active_list.py tests/gateway/test_session_list_live_hidden.py tests/gateway/test_session_list_allowed_sources.py tests/gateway/test_session_aut

## What does this PR do?

When the desktop resolves its Hermes backend through the `HERMES_DESKTOP_HERMES` deployment override, rung 3 of `resolveHermesBackend()` returned a `kind: 'command'` backend **without `root`**. `ticketRuntimeFor()` only mints gateway tickets from (a) a `python` backend with `shell: false`, or (b) a `command` backend that names its installation root (launcher probe cwd + `PYTHONPATH`) — so an override-pinned backend could never bootstrap a gateway ticket, and every desktop → gateway HTTP request through `nativeGatewayHttpHeaders` failed with:

```
Gateway ticket bootstrap requires the installed Hermes Python runtime
```

The app window opened and the backend `serve`d fine, but config / config-defaults / profiles-sidebar (and every other REST call) died for as long as the override was set.

This PR attaches the install directory the launcher itself reports: `launcherInstallDirectory()` (already used by the updater's `userLauncherInstallRoot()` for the exact same `--version` → `Install directory:` contract, and already handling the Windows `.cmd`-via-`cmd.exe` invocation safely) now also feeds the override backend's `root`. The probe is memoized per launcher path — `resolveHermesBackend()` runs once per surface (startup, TUI resume, config refresh, pool backends), and an install directory cannot move while the process lives. If a launcher reports no install directory, `root` stays `undefined` and behavior is unchanged from today.

Fixes #138793

## What

Updates held across a Telegram disconnect are now replayed in the order they arrived.

Before, the hold queue appended in hold order. An update that arrived behind the delivery fence was
held at once, while batches buffered before the fence were held later (own flush, cancelled flush or
teardown salvage), so the reconnect drain replayed the newer update first. An interrupted replay had
the same problem with its re-held remainder.

## How

- Each update gets a process-wide arrival position on first contact in the three enqueue paths
  (text, photo burst, album). A batch keeps its first update's position.
- `_hold_inbound_event` inserts by that position instead of appending; unstamped events keep append
  order. The counter is process-wide so positions stay comparable when a replacement adapter adopts
  its predecessor's queue (#132829).
- The teardown salvage loop moves into the held-inbound mixin, so `adapter.py` does not grow
  (7318 → 7317 lines).

## Tests

New `tests/gateway/test_telegram_held_inbound_order.py`: 11 cases, all failing on `main` @ ca069e12
and passing here.
- all 9 pairs of (buffered-before-fence kind × arrived-after-fence kind) for text / photo burst / album;
- teardown salvage across kinds keeps arrival order;
- an interrupted replay keeps its remaining updates ahead of one that arrived during the interruption.

`scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/ tests/plugins/test_telegram_update_admission.py`: same 13 failures
as `main` on this macOS host (local system proxy / DNS, plus one load-sensitive timing test), no new
failures. `scripts/check --base main`: 12
checks ok, code health 0 findings.

Tested on macOS 26 (Apple silicon), Python 3.14. Not tested against a live Telegram bot;
python-telegram-bot is not installed in this environment (the admission tests skip, as in CI).

---

Opened as a draft only because non-draft creation is currently capped for this account (#131859); the change is complete and ready for review.
