## What does this PR do?

Adds `git-autosave` to the plugin catalog: a lightweight, local alternative to directory checkpoints for people
who mostly work in Git repositories.

Directory checkpoints keep a separate snapshot store per working directory. On large or busy projects that store
is costly to maintain (#135009, #122551, #136935), and #125623 asks for a way to exclude directories from it. This
plugin reuses each project's own Git object database instead:

- Before a mutating tool call (`write_file`, `patch`, common mutating terminal commands), it saves the affected
  repository's working state to `refs/hermes-autosave/<branch>` with a reflog, through a private index. HEAD,
  branches, the real index and the working tree are never touched, and nothing is pushed.
- Outside Git it copies only the existing file about to change.
- `hermes autosave find <file>` lists pre-edit versions; `hermes autosave restore <file>` writes only that path.
- Dependency directories are always skipped, and credential stores are never read or copied.

It does not cover non-Git directories the way checkpoints do; the README says when to keep checkpoints on.

**How it differs from `git-hook`:** `git-hook` commits and pushes real branches every turn. `git-autosave` writes a
private local ref, never commits to a branch and never pushes. It is recovery history, not sync.

The repository owner submits this entry (rule 5). It is pinned to the `v0.3.0` release commit
`b4b12d6bf79318c6708ab468327d52e7671d63f9`.

## Related Issue

None for the entry itself. The checkpoint issues above are the motivation.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `plugin-catalog/git-autosave.yaml` (new; the only file changed).

## Disclosure (rule 13)

- Runs local `git` subprocesses in repositories the agent touches, with hooks, clean filters, fsmonitor,
  split-index and lazy fetch disabled.
- Writes shadow refs and reflogs into those repositories' `.git`, and file copies into its plugin-data directory.
  Both are local and unencrypted.
- Skips credential stores (`.env`, `auth.json`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, `.docker`, `.kube`, gh/gcloud/azure configs) and
  dependency directories, including through symlinks. Repositories with mirror remotes or `refs/*` push refspecs
  are skipped.
- `hermes autosave sweep` reads the Hermes session database read-only. The plugin schedules nothing; the README
  shows how to schedule the sweep yourself.

## What does this PR do?

On native Windows, every Hermes startup prints `Install GitHub Copilot CLI? (y/N):` in the user's terminal when all three of these hold:

- The real Copilot CLI (`@github/copilot`) is not installed, so the wrapper offers to install it.
- `copilot-acp` counts as authenticated (here because `~/.copilot/config.json` holds `copilotTokens`), so the model-picker warm-up asks it for live models.

Call path, traced with a `sys.addaudithook` on `subprocess.Popen` during a real startup:

```
model_switch_providers._warm -> list_authenticated_providers -> _lap_overlay_rows
 -> models._copilot_catalog -> plugins/model-providers/copilot-acp fetch_models
 -> CopilotACPClient.list_models -> _session -> _spawn -> _acp_supported
 -> subprocess.run([...\copilotCli\copilot.BAT, "--help"])
```

**Where the bug shows up:** `agent/copilot_acp_client.py::_acp_supported` calls `subprocess.run` without `creationflags`, so the PowerShell child attaches to the user's console. PowerShell's `Read-Host` writes the prompt straight to that console, even though stdout is captured and stdin is `DEVNULL`. The `Popen` in `_spawn()` right next to it already passes `windows_hide_flags()` (#56747). The docstring of `windows_hide_flags()` covers exactly this case ("short-lived synchronous helpers (... version probes)"). This PR passes the same flag to the check.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged. Output is still captured, and the result is the same: `False` for this wrapper, whose `--help` output has no `--acp`. On non-Windows hosts `windows_hide_flags()` is `0`.

**What the user sees:** this prompt appears every time Hermes starts, right under the banner and before the first message can be typed. Here the user's first message (`my inbox`) was typed into the prompt line:

![Install GitHub Copilot CLI? (y/N) prompt shown on Hermes startup](https://github.com/mtuntang/hermes-agent/blob/pr-assets/pr-138782/copilot-prompt-on-startup.png?raw=true)

## Related Issue

No existing issue. I searched PRs and issues for `_acp_supported`, `copilot.bat`, `copilotCli`, `copilot --help`, "Install GitHub Copilot CLI" and "copilot acp console".

Related:
- #87308 introduced the `--acp` check.
- #133605 (open) also edits
title: fix(acp): stop the 'Install GitHub Copilot CLI?' prompt on Windows startup

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

The Desktop SSH remote bootstrap probes the remote Hermes version with `hermes --version` and reported the **first line** of the merged output as the version. Because the probe appended `2>&1`, any remote stderr warning printed while the CLI started became the "version": in the linked issue, a plugin warning about a missing CLI dependency on the non-interactive SSH PATH was logged as `remote hermes version:` 5,070 times over two weeks, and the real version string never appeared.

Two changes in `probeHermesVersion` (`apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.ts`):

1. **Drop the `2>&1` merge.** `SshConnection.exec()` returns `result.stdout` only (`runSsh` collects stdout and stderr in separate buffers), so remote stderr now stays out of the probe result instead of being spliced ahead of the version line.
2. **Pick the version line, not the first line.** As a second line of defense against stdout noise (shell banners, login echoes), the probe now returns the first line starting with `Hermes Agent v` and only falls back to the first line when no such line exists — preserving the old behavior for unexpected/unrecognized version strings.

All consumers of the probe result (`remote hermes version:` log line, lockfile `hermesVersion`, the `${version} at ${path}` connection summary) are display-only, so the narrower extraction cannot break any version comparison logic.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138772

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.ts` — `probeHermesVersion` no longer appends `2>&1` to the remote `--version` command (stderr stays on the ssh stderr channel), and returns the first line matching `Hermes Agent v` instead of blindly taking the first output line.
- `apps/desktop/electron/remote-lifecycle.test.ts` — regression test: a noisy probe output (a leading non-version warning line followed by the real version line) resolves to the version line, and the probe command itself no longer contains `--version 2>&1`. The watchdog sleeper's own `2>&1` redirection (part of `withRemoteTimeout`, unchanged) is unaffected.

author: snowzlmbot
body:
## Problem

Fixes #35932. Custom providers with mixed-case slugs (e.g. `MyGateway`, `BitFun`, any provider whose key in `providers:` contains uppercase letters) are silently dropped from the Telegram `/model` inline keyboard. All-lowercase providers are unaffected.

### Root cause

`group_providers()` lowercases every slug before returning it (`models_catalog_static.py:479`):
```python
s = str(slug or "").strip().lower()
```

But `_build_provider_keyboard` built `by_slug` with the original mixed-case slug as the key (`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:4410` before this fix):
```python
by_slug = {p.get("slug"): p for p in providers}  # key = original case
```

Then looked up using the lowercased slug from `group_providers()`:
```python
p = by_slug.get(row["slug"])  # key = lowercased — never matches
```

The lookup always returns `None` for mixed-case slugs, so the button is silently dropped.

### Why previous PRs (#35933, #35953, #37282) did not fix this

All three targeted `gateway/platforms/telegram.py`, which is the **retired** gateway adapter. The active code path is `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`. The triage comment on #35932 identifies this: _"All three diffs currently target the retired gateway adapter rather than the active Telegram plugin path."_

This PR targets the correct file.

## Fix

Normalize the `by_slug` key to lowercase so it matches what `group_providers()` returns:

```python
# Before
by_slug = {p.get("slug"): p for p in providers}

# After  
by_slug = {(p.get("slug") or "").lower(): p for p in providers}
```

The original slug is still stored on the provider dict and appears in callback data (`mp:<slug>`), so the round-trip selection path is unaffected.

## Verification

Simulation of the exact keyboard-build loop before and after the fix, using the real `group_providers()` function, confirmed the bug and the fix:

**Before fix (simulated):**
```
picker slugs:              ['pipioClaude', 'pipio', 'deepseek']
group_providers() returns: ['pipioclaude', 'pipio', 'deepseek']  ← lowercased
by_slug keys:              ['pipioClaude', 'pipio', 'deepseek']  ← original case
BUTTONS SHOWN:             ['pipio', 'deepseek']
DROPPED:                   ['pipioclaude']  ← pipioClaude silently dropped
```

**After fix:**
```
BUTTONS SHOWN: ['pipioclaude', 'pipio', 'deepseek']
DROPPED:       []
```

The regression test in `tests/plugins/platforms/telegram/test_model_picker_case_mismatch.py` covers:
- All-lowercase slugs (baseline)
- The

author: teknium1
body:
The Desktop Artifacts page now lists files the agent links with CommonMark angle-bracket destinations (paths with spaces) and labels Windows paths by their file name.

Port of [block/buzz#8168](https://github.com/block/buzz/pull/8168) ("preserve Markdown attachment destinations": angle-bracketed URLs, spaces, parentheses, optional titles), adapted from their Flutter link normalizer to our Artifacts scraper.

## Changes
- `apps/desktop/src/app/artifacts/artifact-utils.ts`: Markdown image/link scraping parses the destination like CommonMark: `<...>` (spaces allowed) or a bare run with one level of balanced parens, then an optional `"title"` / `'title'`. It was `\(([^)\s]+)\)`, so `![chart](</home/u/My Pictures/q3 chart.png>)` never matched, and the prose path fallback cannot see a path that starts after `<`.
- `artifactLabel`: Windows paths take their basename before URL parsing. `new URL('C:\\x\\y.png')` accepts `c:` as a scheme and keeps the backslashes, so every Windows artifact was labelled `\x\y.png`.
- 2 invariant tests (`markdown-destinations.test.ts`), both red on `origin/main`.

Root cause: chat rendering got angle-bracket destinations in #130020 (#102782), but the Artifacts page has its own regex scraper and was left behind. This PR fixes that second surface.

## Validation

**Live repro (real Electron app + real `hermes serve`, scripted provider via the `e2e/core` harness):** one assistant turn replying with `![chart](</home/u/My Pictures/q3 chart.png>)`, `[report](<~/Reports/Q3 (final).pdf>)`, `![render](<C:\Users\me\My Renders\frame 01.webp>)`, `![logo](/srv/out/logo.png "Company logo")`, then open Artifacts and read the DOM:

| Tree | Artifacts page tabs | Listed |
|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | All 1 · Images 1 · Files 0 | `logo.png` only |
| this PR | All 4 · Images 3 · Files 1 | `q3 chart.png`, `frame 01.webp`, `logo.png`, `Q3 (final).pdf` |

- `vitest run src/app/artifacts/`: 33/33 (3 files). New tests: 2/2 red on base, green on head.
- `tsc -p . --noEmit`, eslint on touched files, `scripts/check --only health`: clean.

## Ours vs theirs
| | Buzz #8168 | Hermes before | Hermes after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chat render of `<...>` destinations | fixed (mobile) | already handled (#130020) | unchanged |
| Secondary index of attachments | gallery/video/file routing | Artifacts page dropped them | parsed per CommonMark |
| Titles / balanced parens | handled | handled by fallback path scan | handled by the primary parser |

Not ported: Buzz's image
title: fix(desktop): Artifacts page lists files linked with spaced paths (port block/buzz#8168)

author: MoBluey
body:
## What does this PR do?

Gives a turn one retry when the streaming guard cuts a runaway loop in the reasoning channel, instead of ending on "Repetition Detected".

`main` already cuts a live repetition loop mid-stream (`RunawayStreamWatch` in `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`) and marks the response `_runaway_repetition = True`. `recover_from_truncation` then ends the turn whichever channel looped. That's right for the visible content channel - a continuation walks straight back into the loop. For the reasoning channel it throws the turn away before the model has answered. It's deliberating in circles, and a fresh request telling it to stop usually gets an answer or a tool call.

- The runaway mark now carries the cut channel (`"content"` or `"reasoning"`) instead of `True`, on both the chat_completions and anthropic stream paths. Still truthy, so the existing check is unchanged.
- On a reasoning-channel cut, `recover_from_truncation` drops the partial, appends a one-line wrap-up nudge ("Your reasoning started repeating itself and was cut off. Stop deliberating; act now with a tool call or give your answer.") and restarts the request. One retry per turn (`_reasoning_runaway_retries`, reset per turn). A second reasoning loop, or any content loop, ends the turn as before, and the looped text never reaches the stored messages.

### Related work

- #78807 (open issue): DeepSeek V4 Flash reasoning loops that run until the user steps in. `main` already cuts them. This PR turns the first cut into one recovery attempt instead of a failed turn.
- #125650 (open): cuts a looping visible stream at 8k-char thresholds via `interrupt()` in `agent/stream_delivery.py`. Different channel, different files, no overlap.
- #117756 (open): cuts degenerate thinking-stream runs inside `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py` and keeps the turn alive by trimming the reasoning. Not tested together. They should compose - a #117756 trim keeps the stream going, and this retry only fires after the runaway watch has cut it. Both edit `chat_completion_helpers.py`, so whichever lands second needs a rebase.

## Related Issue

Refs #78807. Reduces the impact of a cut reasoning loop, doesn't stop models looping.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix (undisclosed vulnerabilities in [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/SECURITY.md) §3.1 scope
title: fix(agent): retry a reasoning-channel runaway once with a wrap-up nudge

author: MoBluey
body:
## What does this PR do?

Rejects `terminal` and `execute_code` calls with an empty or bare no-op payload before dispatch, with an error telling the model to send the real call.

A stalling model (mostly local models over chat_completions) sometimes sends `{"command": ":"}`, `{"command": ""}` or `{"code": "pass"}` instead of the command it meant to run. Dispatch ran it, it "succeeded" with no output, and the model had no signal nothing happened. It either repeated the same empty call or ended the turn thinking the work ran.

`handle_function_call` now checks the payload argument for these two tools only:

- `terminal.command`: missing, blank, or exactly `:`, `true`, `/bin/true`, `/usr/bin/true`, `exit 0`
- `execute_code.code`: missing, blank, or exactly `pass`, `...`, `None`

On a match it returns a tool error naming the tool and argument ("terminal was called with the bare no-op ':' as `command`, so nothing ran. Re-emit the complete terminal call with the actual command you intend to run in the `command` argument.") and fires `post_tool_call` with `status="blocked"`, `error_type="noop_tool_args"`. Everything else dispatches as before, including commands starting with `:` (`: > file`) and `true` inside a pipeline. Both arguments are already `required` in the tool schemas, so a valid call never has them empty.

## Related Issue

No existing issue found. Happy to file one if preferred.

Related, not a duplicate: #43259 guards a `None` command inside `tools/terminal_tool.py`. This PR works at dispatch, covers `execute_code` too, and catches no-op payloads, not just missing ones.

author: MoBluey
body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops a turn ending on a visible line that announces the next step after the agent has already run tools.

Once a turn has a tool result in its history, `looks_like_codex_intermediate_ack()` returns `False`. That leaves `trailing_continue_intent()` as the only catch, and it only knows `let me now` / `I'll now` / `next, I` and gives up past 400 chars. Lines like "I can proceed with the first fix using the terminal tool." or "Let me write the parse script to a file first, then run it." after a tool round ended the turn as if they were the answer.

Two changes. Both feed the existing stall branch in `finish_text_response`, under the shared two-nudge cap.

1. `trailing_continue_intent()` also matches an unconditional `I can proceed ...` tail. Conditions either side ("if you confirm", "once you approve", "pending your approval", "with your go-ahead", "you decide") still end the turn. The length cap goes from 400 to 600 chars so a short progress summary before the announcement still counts. Applies to every model.
2. `visible_reply_announces_action()` runs the existing promoted-reasoning plan-tail check on visible text, for models opted in to intent-ack continuation (`agent.intent_ack_continuation: true` or a list entry matching the model). It screens the last sentence for sign-offs ("let me know", "I'll wait", "I'll be here"), offers ("if you want") and conditions first. Works with or without prior tool results.

Against the examples in #122119:

| Visible reply | `trailing_continue_intent` | `visible_reply_announces_action` (opted-in models) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `I will continue the inventory and fix the defect.` | False | True |
| `I'll fix the defect now.` | False | True |
| `Let me check the remaining files.` | False | True |
| `Next I will run the tests.` | False | True |
| 458-char progress report ending `I will now fix the defect.` | True (was False) | True |
| German / French continuations | False | False |

The stall detectors (`trailing_continue_intent`, `promoted_reasoning_announces_action` and the new code) move to `agent/agent_runtime_helpers_stall_intent.py` to keep `agent/agent_runtime_helpers.py` under its size cap. `finish_text_response` calls one helper, `announces_unfinished_action()`, to stay under its line cap. No behaviour change from the move. Callers and tests import from the new module, no re-export shim (per AGENTS.md).

### Related work

- #78113 (open) adds `agent/false_stop.py` with two post-tool signatu
title: fix(agent): nudge a stall line that follows a tool round (#122119)

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

A credential removed with `hermes auth remove` comes back when any long-running Hermes process that loaded the pool *before* the removal writes the pool again (rotation, cooldown, status change). The root cause is that `write_credential_pool`'s `removed_ids` parameter only filters that single write's disk merge-back — nothing records that a row was deliberately removed, so a process whose in-memory snapshot still holds the row writes it back verbatim.

This PR makes removals durable: `write_credential_pool` records rows passed via `removed_ids` as id → timestamp tombstones in a new `credential_pool_removals` section of auth.json, and every subsequent write drops rows whose id is tombstoned. Tombstones expire after 7 days (a stale process is expected to flush well within that window; expiry keeps the section from growing unboundedly). Re-adding a credential mints a fresh uuid id, so `auth add` is unaffected by an old tombstone.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138756

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/auth.py` — `write_credential_pool` now registers `removed_ids` as removal tombstones (id → epoch) in the store, filters tombstoned ids out of every write's final row list (both caller entries and the merge-back branch), and garbage-collects tombstones older than the 7-day TTL.
- `hermes_cli/auth_pool_merge.py` — verbatim move of the pool-row merge helpers (`_POOL_STATUS_FIELDS`, `_POOL_TOKEN_GENERATION_FIELDS`, `_credential_token_pair`, `_token_pairs_by_id`, `_merge_pool_row_generation`, `_merge_disk_cooldown_state`, `_entry_ids`) out of `hermes_cli/auth.py`, re-exported from their old home so every caller and monkeypatch path keeps working. This keeps `auth.py` under its FILE_LINES cap alongside the fix (code health ratchet: 0 blocking).
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_pool_removal_tombstone.py` — new regression tests: stale-process resurrection, concurrently-added row kept, re-added credential with a fresh id survives, expired tombstone stops filtering and is dropped, plain write creates no tombstone section.

## How to Test

1. Run the self-contained reproduction from the issue against this branch (throwaway `HERMES_HOME`, calls `write_credential_pool` directly):
   ```python
   write_credential_pool("openrouter", [row("keep"), row("revoked")])
   write_credential_pool("openrouter", [row("keep")], removed_ids=["revoked"])  # hermes auth remove
   write_credential_poo
title: fix(auth): tombstone removed pool rows so stale processes cannot write them back

author: shariqriazz
body:
## What does this PR do?

During `hermes update`, the new code is installed before the running gateway is replaced. If a cron job fires in that window, the old gateway's ticker spawns a restart-safe external worker, and that worker runs the new code. The worker finds its own parent gateway as the owner, sees it as an older runtime it isn't allowed to stop, and books the run as FAILED:

```
GatewayUnavailableError: Gateway incompatible: runtime_protocol (an older Hermes gateway owns this profile and was not verified; run: hermes gateway stop)
```

The suggested remedy doesn't fit either: the caller is a child of that gateway, and the update restarts the gateway anyway.

With this change, the worker waits for the replacement gateway instead of failing. This follows the rule `cron/scheduler_gateway_gate.py` already applies to headless ticks: a slot lost to a restart window is a missed fire, not a job failure.

The wait is deliberately narrow. `incompatible/runtime_protocol` is also used for a newer owner, a foreign install and an unverified or recycled pid, and a plain `draining` or `starting` can mean an operator drain or a hung owner. So the fix doesn't retry on those. It adds a structured reason for the one case that is known to resolve itself:

- `replace_incompatible_owner` now reports `owner_is_parent` when the owner pid is this process's parent, instead of folding it into `owner_unverified`.
- `ensure_gateway_runtime` maps that to `incompatible` with `reason_code="parent_outdated"`.
- `GatewayUnavailableError` carries the `reason_code`.

The worker waits only when all of these hold:

- the verdict is `incompatible/parent_outdated` or `draining/update_paused` (the update fence);
- the process is the external worker for this execution, and it was dispatched as `scoped`, which is the only mode that survives the gateway restart;
- nothing has been submitted yet, and the job hasn't been cancelled.

The wait is capped at 900 s. Execution progress is touched while it waits. Cancellation and the deadline are checked before every dial, and when the wait ends without a ready gateway, the original error is raised as before. Interactive callers, `degraded` workers and in-process dispatch (Windows/macOS) still fail fast.

## Related Issue

Refs #134889 (report: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889#issuecomment-6182345464), a follow-up to #106742.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

title: fix(cron): scoped worker waits out an update's gateway handover instead of failing

## What does this PR do?

`execute_code`'s `_build_child_env()` scrubbed the child environment and only re-injected `TZ` from **Hermes' own timezone setting** (`HERMES_TIMEZONE` → `config.yaml: timezone`). The `TZ` the operator passed to the container was never consulted — it is not in the scrub allowlist either. A Docker deployment that sets `TZ` (the universal container idiom) and nothing else ended up with **two clocks in one container**: the sandbox child resolved local time from the image's system zone (`Etc/UTC`) while `terminal`, cron scripts and the supervised gateway in the same container followed `TZ`, silently off by the host offset (#138741).

The fix gives `TZ` the same inheritance semantics as `PATH`/`HOME`/`LANG` — it describes the deployment's locale and the sandbox is a subprocess of an already-configured container — while keeping an explicitly configured Hermes `timezone` authoritative. The pass-through is **exact-name**: glibc's `TZDIR`, a different variable that merely shares the prefix, stays scrubbed.

Precedence in `_build_child_env`: Hermes-configured timezone → inherited `TZ` → system local time (unchanged). Windows keeps its existing behavior (#112233): no `TZ` injection at all, the OS-configured zone stays authoritative.

## Related Issue

author: enckequity
body:
## What does this PR do?

Dashboard console commands (`/api/console`) now go through the retirement fence. Before this, `chat_ws.run_command` submitted each line straight to the console executor. `RetirementFence.prepare()` couldn't see a running command (for example `curator run`, which forks an agent and calls the provider), so it could grant a permit and the backend got stopped mid-command.

The command now reserves admission before it is queued and releases it from the worker future's done callback. That's the same pattern `tools/async_delegation.py` uses. The reservation tracks the worker thread, not the waiter: after a cancel or timeout, `_unwind_console_worker` can stop waiting while the thread is still running, and the fence stays held until the thread exits. A command that arrives while admission is closed gets the usual error frame ("Hermes backend is retiring and accepts no new commands; reconnect to continue") and a `complete` frame with status `error`. The engine never runs it.

## Related Issue

Part of #138750 (item 1).

## What does this PR do?

Selecting text inside a chat message now offers a floating **Add to chat** action at the selection. Pressing it inserts the passage into the composer as a bracketed markdown blockquote, so the follow-up question is visibly about that snippet — and the agent receives the quote as explicit context instead of a bare sentence with no anchor.

**The gap this closes:** the desktop already has exactly this affordance for *terminal and file-preview* selections (⌘/Ctrl+L → the `@terminal:` chip path), but nothing for the transcript. Asking about part of a long reply today means retyping or pasting the text, which loses the anchor entirely.

**Why this approach:** the pieces already exist upstream — the composer's programmatic insert bus (`requestComposerInsert` / `requestComposerFocus` in `app/chat/composer/focus.ts`) and stable message roots (`data-slot="aui_assistant-message-root"`). So this adds a pure capture rule plus a floating action and reuses that bus: **no new RPC, no backend change, no new store, no editor internals.** The passage travels as draft text, so per-session draft stashing, undo, copy/paste and the existing selection behaviour keep working untouched.

author: teknium1
body:
`hermes doctor --turn` runs one real agent turn on the configured main model, so a route that answers `/models` but cannot actually chat no longer reports green.

## Why

Doctor's connectivity section and `--live` only GET provider `/models` endpoints. A route can pass all of them and still fail every chat: a model slug the provider does not serve, an account without access to the model, a request shape the provider rejects, or a model that answers but never calls tools. Users find out on their first message.

## Changes

- New `hermes_cli/doctor_turn.py` sibling + `--turn` flag (opt-in; a few small model requests, about 2-4 and capped at 6 iterations, so it never runs by default).
- Resolution is the `hermes -z` path (`_resolve_model_and_provider` → `resolve_runtime_provider`) with the **fallback chain off**: a healthy fallback would otherwise hide a dead primary.
- Only the `todo` toolset is exposed, context files / memory / background review are skipped, and the agent runs with `_persist_disabled`, so no session row is written.
- Verdict follows the `-z` exit-code rules (`_oneshot_exit_code`): a failed / partial / interrupted turn is a FAIL even when it left explanatory text in `final_response`. A turn that answers without running the tool is a WARN (tool calling unreliable on this route). The row shows provider/model, API mode, wall time and tokens.
- The tool call is judged on the tool-RESULT row, because with deferred tools the model reaches `todo_list` through the `tool_call` dispatcher (found in the live run: an assistant-side name check read a working round trip as "never called").
- Docs: `cli-commands.md` doctor section now lists `--live` and `--turn`.

author: jquesnelle
body:
Two log lines misled while testing #138560 on an RTX Spark. This PR fixes both.

**The heartbeat blamed sleep on the GIL.** Every lid close logged a warning that named the wrong cause:

```
WARNING hermes_cli.web_server: event loop stalled 229.5s (GIL pressure suspected)
INFO agent.chat_completion_stream_monitor: Computer slept for 229s during a model request; ...
```

The web server's heartbeat measures how late its 2 s tick runs, using the monotonic clock. On Windows that clock counts sleep, so a sleep looks like a stall. The heartbeat now compares the process's CPU time across the late tick:

- A GIL stall keeps some thread busy, so the CPU time grows.
- A sleeping computer, or a process frozen by Modern Standby, uses none.

A late tick with an idle process now logs `event loop paused Ns with the process idle (the computer was probably asleep)` at INFO. A late tick with a busy process keeps the existing warning, with its exact wording unchanged. The heartbeat moves out of the `web_server` facade into `web_server_lifecycle`.

**The hardware poll logged the same line every 5 s.** The statusbar's system-resources item polls `/api/local-models/hardware` every 5 s while it is shown. On unified memory, each poll logged the allocator pool reading at INFO: 12 identical lines a minute. The reading is now logged once, and again whenever it changes. The poll's single shared `nvidia-smi` read (#120262) is unchanged.

**Tests:** `tests/hermes_cli/test_sleep_aware_log_lines.py` covers:

- a punctual tick, a sleep and a busy stall;
- a late tick going through the armed heartbeat;
- one pool line across 12 polls, and another line after the reading changes.

`scripts/check` passes 12/12. The `tests/hermes_cli/test_web_server*.py` and `test_local_*.py` runs show the same 15 failures on `release/0.22.1` without this change.
title: fix(local): stop two log lines from misleading on a sleeping laptop

author: enckequity
body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes cron status` and `hermes doctor` already probe whether a profile's cron store accepts writes (`cron/store_health.py::probe_report`) and report a full disk, read-only mount or wrong owner. The dashboard and desktop app can't see any of that. A hosted or multi-profile operator who only has the HTTP surface finds out once jobs stop firing.

This adds `GET /api/cron/store-health?profile=<name>`, which runs the same probe against the selected profile's store and returns:

```json
{"profile": "worker", "writable": true, "unwritable": null}
```

When the store is unwritable, `writable` is `false` and `unwritable` carries the same `store` / `error` / `since` / `fix` fields the CLI prints. The probe is a cross-process write test, so it works from the dashboard process no matter which process owns the ticker. Like the other cron routes, it runs off the event loop via `_run_cron_dashboard_io` and resolves the profile through `_cron_profile_home` (unknown profile -> 404).

## Related Issue

No existing issue. This is a small read-only extension of the store-health work merged in #133283.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/web_server_cron.py`: `_cron_store_health_sync(profile)` runs `probe_report` on the profile's cron dir inside `_cron_store_scope`.
- `hermes_cli/web_routers/cron.py`: `GET /api/cron/store-health` route.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_cron_store_health_route.py` (new): healthy store, an unwritable store probed under the selected profile's dir, and an unknown profile returning 404.
- `website/docs/user-guide/features/web-dashboard.md`: documents the endpoint and adds it to the profile-scoped endpoint list.

## What does this PR do?

A stale `platform_toolsets.cli` entry (a toolset whose plugin was uninstalled) no longer makes every `hermes chat` fail with `Hermes couldn't start the model connection: invalid_params`. The CLI warns `Unknown toolsets: …` and carries on, as it did before #106742.

With no `-t`, `_build_cli_from_args` resolved the profile's default toolsets on the client (`_get_platform_tools(CLI_CONFIG, "cli")`, stale name included) and `_ensure_gateway_session` / `/new` sent that list as `session.create` `toolsets`. The gateway treats any `toolsets` it receives as the user's explicit pick and refuses unknown names with `invalid_params` (`gateway/session_policy.py::_resolve_toolsets`), which is its documented contract (`gateway-local-sessions.md`: "Unknown or policy-filtered toolsets reject instead of silently disappearing"). So the gateway was right; the client was sending a default as if it were a choice.

This change sends `toolsets` only when the list is a real pick, and leaves the profile default to the gateway:

| Launch | `toolsets` sent, before | `toolsets` sent, after | Result after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hermes chat` with a stale `platform_toolsets.cli` entry | the resolved default, stale name included | none | session created; CLI prints `Unknown toolsets` |
| `/new` in that session | the resolved default | none | session created |
| `hermes chat -t terminal,bogus` | `[terminal, bogus]` | `[terminal, bogus]` | still refused (`invalid_params`) |
| coding-posture workspace (no `-t`) | the posture list | the posture list | unchanged |

Fixes #138670. Thanks @smerther-create for the report.

## What does this PR do?

A hosted-room member turn that carries a bound file no longer dies as an ambiguous attempt on routes that can't carry files. Those routes now refuse the turn by name **before** submit, so it settles as a failure instead of sitting in `running`.

`HostedRoomRuntime._execute_attempt` forwards `attachments=` to every member transport, but only the canonical `HostedRoomAuthorityRPC` (and its `HostedRoomOwnerRPC` subclass) accepts it. The legacy in-process `HostedRoomServerRPC` and `PeerHostedRoomTransport` raise `TypeError` after `submit_attempted` is set, so the driver books the attempt ambiguous.

| Route | Turn with a file, before | Turn with a file, after | Turn without a file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Canonical (`HostedRoomAuthorityRPC` / `HostedRoomOwnerRPC`) | runs, file resolved per member | unchanged | unchanged |
| Legacy in-process (`HostedRoomServerRPC`) | `TypeError` → ambiguous, task stays `running` | settles failed: `attachments_unsupported_on_route` | unchanged |
| Peer (`PeerHostedRoomTransport`) | `TypeError` → ambiguous, task stays `running` | settles failed: `attachments_unsupported_on_route` | unchanged |

Before the unified-gateway merge the legacy route dropped the file silently and answered without it. A named refusal is deliberate here: a turn that runs without its file is worse than one that says why it didn't run.

author: benbarclay
body:
## Summary

Since the unified gateway runtime ([#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742)), a relay message routed to a profile by the connector is **acknowledged and silently dropped**. This happens when the connector stamps `source.profile`, which is how Team Gateway per-scope profile routing works. The gateway never runs the turn and never replies. Because the connector got an ack, it never redelivers either.

This PR restores delivery on both single-profile and multiplexed gateways.

## Background for reviewers

The relay connector fronts a shared bot for many tenants. For an instance with profile routes, it decides which Hermes profile serves each inbound event and stamps that profile name on `source.profile` before sending the event down the gateway's relay WebSocket. Before #106742, `resolve_identity` used the stamp on a multiplexed gateway (the turn ran under that profile's home and `agent:<profile>` namespace). A single-profile gateway ignored it.

After #106742, relay text no longer goes through `handle_message`. `RelayAdapter._on_inbound` goes straight to native admission: `admit_producer` → `prepare_native` → `capture_provenance` → `_binding`. `_binding` works out the runtime profile only from the gateway's **local** `profile_routes` (plus explicit `/p/<profile>` webhook/API prefixes). It never looks at the connector's stamp. As a result:

- **Multiplexed gateway, stamp names a non-primary profile:** `(source.profile or primary) != runtime_profile` raises `profile_mismatch`.
- **Single-profile gateway, any stamp:** the `not multiplex and source.profile` guard raises `profile_mismatch`.

`profile_mismatch` is in the relay adapter's `_PERMANENT_REFUSALS`, so the frame is acked and dropped. The only trace is the warning `relay inbound refused (profile_mismatch) … acknowledged, not replayed`.

The cross-repo connector E2E suite doesn't catch this. Its drivers exercise the relay transport, not a gateway runner with a session authority. All 38 drivers pass on current `main`.

## Change

- **`gateway/session_ingress_context.py` (`_binding`, multiplex branch, via the new `_runtime_profile` helper):** a relay-delivered `source.profile` is treated as the route.
  - It is trusted because the relay flag comes only from the authenticated WS reader, or from a verified seal on restore. The seal is an HMAC over `source.to_dict()`, which includes `profile`, so editing the profile in a stored admission cannot reroute it.
  - The stamp wi

author: khangnhh
body:
## Symptom

Scheduled jobs began failing on every tick, three retries each, then a job-level `RuntimeError`:

```
HTTP 504: Error 504: Gateway time-out
  "error_name": "origin_gateway_timeout", "error_code": 504,
  "retryable": true, "retry_after": 120, "owner_action_required": true
```

Every attempt took ~90 s and failed identically, across different jobs and repeated runs. Interactive
requests to the same endpoint succeeded throughout (including a 212k-token request in ~10 s), so it was
not load, not prompt size, and not the job's own prompt.

## Root cause

Replaying the exact request body — Hermes writes `request_dump_*.json` on API errors — reproduces the
504 deterministically. Varying `max_tokens`, `stream` and `tools` changes nothing; bisecting the prompt
isolates the trigger to the **hint `_build_job_prompt()` prepends to every cron prompt**:

| user prompt sent | result |
| --- | --- |
| stock hint alone (514 chars) | 504 after 90 s |
| stock hint + a job prompt of `Say hello` | 504 after 90 s |
| same, with `max_tokens=512` / `stream=true` / `tools` removed | 504 |
| the same job prompt with the hint reworded | 200 in ~3 s |
| the same job prompt with the hint removed | 200 in ~3 s |

Because a two-line job fails on the hint alone, the job body is irrelevant: with the old wording, *every*
cron job on an affected model/route fails on every tick.

## Change

Reword `cron_hint` so it no longer reads as a bracket-marker + tool-name imperative block
(`[IMPORTANT: … do NOT use send_message …`). The delivery and silence semantics are unchanged:
the reply is handed to the user by the system, no messaging tool is called by the agent, `[SILENT]`
alone means nothing to report, and `[SILENT]` must never be mixed with real content.

## Verification

- `_build_job_prompt()` output still carries the `[SILENT]` instruction, the auto-delivery rule and the
  job prompt; the previous phrasing is gone.
- Silence contract unchanged (`_is_cron_silence_response()`): `[SILENT]`, `  [SILENT]  `, `SILENT`,
  `NO_REPLY` suppress delivery; `[SILENT]` mid-sentence in a real report still delivers.
- End-to-end replay with the new hint against the affected endpoint: 200 in ~4 s, and the agent still
  starts with its tool calls; a job with nothing to report still answers exactly `[SILENT]`.

## Notes

The endpoint is a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible gateway fronted by Cloudflare, and the 504 body itself
reports `owner_action_required: true` — the origin has a real problem of it
title: fix(cron): reword scheduled-run hint that stalls provider routes past origin timeout

author: thebergerking91
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lets a plugin that starts children through the public subagent lifecycle API display them exactly like `delegate_task` children in Hermes Desktop and the TUI: the inline delegation card, the batch grouped in the Agents panel, a live transcript per child, and the same after a transcript reload.

Today a lifecycle launch builds and runs the child with the same host-owned path as `delegate_task`, but it never gets the batch identity (`delegation_id`, `task_index` / `task_count`) or a live transcript, and the tool call that launched it renders as a generic tool row because the delegation card is keyed on the literal name `delegate_task`. A plugin cannot fix that from its side: the live transcript writers and the delegation id are private delegation helpers, and the Desktop card is a static name list.

Two small, declarative additions:

1. **`SubagentLifecycleService.launch_batch(requests)`** starts several children as ONE delegation, the way a multi-task `delegate_task` call does. The host mints the `delegation_id`, stamps `task_index` / `task_count`, and creates one live transcript per child with the exact helpers `delegate_task` uses (`create_live_transcripts`, the new `_attach_live_delegation`, `update_manifest_statuses`). Every request is validated and routed before any child is built, so one bad request starts nothing. `launch(request)` is now a batch of one, so single launches get the transcript too.
2. **`register_tool(..., ui_card="delegate")`** (registry + `PluginContext`). The gateway treats a tool that declared a card like the built-in card tools: its `tool.start` / `tool.complete` lifecycle is always emitted (also with `display.tool_progress: off`) and both payloads, plus rehydrated history tool rows, carry `card: "delegate"`. Desktop learns the mapping from the first event or history row that carries it and renders the `delegate_task` card for that tool, live and after reload.

`delegate_task` itself is unchanged in behavior; the only touch is the extraction of `_attach_live_delegation` so both paths share one implementation.

Motivating plugin: seppegadeyne/hermes-claude-agents#1 (named Claude subagents via the lifecycle API). The plugin's matching change feature-detects both additions and keeps working on older builds.

The autouse live-system guard (`tests/_fixtures/live_system_guard.py`) blocked a mutating `systemctl` verb only when the command named the gateway (`hermes-gateway`, `hermes.service`, `hermes gateway`, ...). `hermes-dashboard*`, `hermes-serve*` and every other Hermes unit got through, so a test that forgot to stub the runner restarted the developer's real units. They stub the old `_finish_dashboard_update_cleanup` hook, but the update now runs `update_cmd_maint._refresh_dashboard_after_update`. Words are split on quotes and shell punctuation too, so `bash -c "systemctl restart hermes-dashboard"` is caught in string form as well as list form. body:
## What does this PR do?

A gateway started through the bundled/Docker payload's `bin/hermes` (`scripts/build/launchers.py::posix_launcher`) is invisible to gateway identity. `live_gateway_pid_for_home()` returns None, the dashboard shows Stopped, and `hermes gateway status` says nothing is running. `hermes gateway stop` can't find the gateway, and `restart` prints "nothing to start" and leaves it running. `hermes gateway migrate` can never confirm. The launcher runs `python -P -c "import os, site, sys; sys.argv[0]='hermes'; site.addsitedir(os.environ['HERMES_SITE']); from hermes_cli.main import main; sys.exit(main())" <argv>`. No `gateway/status_inline_source.py::_BOOTSTRAPS` row knew that shape, so the #107002 guard treated its argv as data.

This salvages #127868 by @dskwe: both commits are cherry-picked with `-x` and keep their authorship. The row now lives in `status_inline_source.py`, where `_BOOTSTRAPS` moved after #127868 was written. A follow-up commit closes two gaps that remained:

- **Matcher precision.** The salvaged row matched `import os, site, sys;.*` plus any `from <module> import <func>`. Its `.*` could span a carrier program's own source plus the launcher argv it carries. The `"hermes_cli.main" in joined` substring check also accepted `not_hermes_cli.main`, `foreign.hermes_cli.main` and `hermes_cli.main_x`. author: teknium1
body:
An Enter or digit that lands the instant a dangerous-command prompt appears (you were sending a message) no longer approves the command in the classic CLI and the Ink TUI; for the first 0.5 s only deny/Esc/view act.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/cli_modal_mixin.py`: the approval state records `shown_at`; `_approval_key_too_early()` swallows allow choices (`once`/`session`/`always`) for `_APPROVAL_KEY_GRACE_S = 0.5`; `_approval_pick()` refuses an early digit **without moving the highlight** (otherwise a later deliberate Enter would commit the stray choice). Enter goes through the same check in `_handle_approval_selection`, and the swallowed Enter is consumed, so the composer text is not submitted either.
- `ui-tui/src/components/prompts.tsx`: `approvalAction(…, ageMs)` returns `noop` for allow keys under `APPROVAL_KEY_GRACE_MS`; `ApprovalPrompt` is keyed by `requestId` in `appOverlays.tsx`, so each queued approval starts its own window and opens on the first choice (also what Muse 1.4.6 fixed: "approval prompts open at the first choice instead of inheriting a previous highlight").
- Docs: `user-guide/security.md` approval-flow paragraph.

Root cause: the default selection is "once", and the panel accepts keys from its first painted frame.

## Source (Muse Code)
Muse Code 1.4.4 changelog (https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog): "Pressing Enter right after answering a permission prompt no longer sends the half-typed message hidden behind it, and a prompt that just appeared ignores Enter, y, p, and number keys for a moment so a stray keystroke can't approve it." Hermes adaptation: deny stays live (a stray deny is harmless, a stray allow is not).

## Validation
Live A/B, real `hermes chat` in tmux (isolated HERMES_HOME, xAI grok-4.20), model asked to `rm -rf <scratch dir>`; the driver sends Enter the moment the panel text appears, then once more 1.5 s later.

|---|---|---|
| Classic CLI, stray Enter | `⚠ Approval: rm -rf …/victim-main → allowed once`, dir deleted | dir intact, panel still open |
| Classic CLI, deliberate Enter 1.5 s later | n/a | `→ allowed once`, dir deleted |

author: teknium1
body:
`find . -exec nice rm {} \;` (or `sudo` / `env` / `timeout` / `doas` / `flock` / `ionice` … in front of `rm`) now asks for approval like the bare `find -exec rm`, instead of deleting every match unprompted.

## Changes
- `tools/approval_detection.py::_find_exec_finding`: every `-exec`/`-execdir` action of a `find` command is parsed and its argv walked through the existing command-position wrapper walker (`_iter_shell_command_word_spans`, same option/positional semantics as top-level `sudo …`). A launched `rm` returns the **same key** as the regex rule (`find -exec/-execdir rm`), so one session approval covers both spellings.
- `-exec {}` / `-exec sh {}` / `-exec python3 {}` (running each matched file as a program) asks too.
- An argument merely named `rm` stays data: `-exec grep rm {} +`, `-exec sudo cat {} +`, `-exec chmod +x {} +` still run.
- `doas` and `flock` join `_COMMAND_WRAPPER_WORDS` (with their argument-taking options), which also closes `doas python3 -c …` at top level.
- Docs: `user-guide/security.md` pattern table row.

Root cause: the `find -exec/-execdir rm` rule is a regex that only matches `rm` immediately after `-exec`.

## Source (Muse Code)
Muse Code 1.4.6 changelog, Security (https://dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/changelog): "Ask me and Auto-review now also ask before running a find -exec that reaches rm or the matched file through sudo, env, setsid, nice, nohup, timeout, stdbuf, time, command or xargs … and before a find -exec that launches rm behind a wrapper they do not otherwise know, such as ionice, doas, flock or chrt … find -exec chmod, mv, sed -i and grep still run without asking (an argument named rm alone does not make them ask)." Hermes adaptation: reuse the one wrapper walker we already trust at command position instead of a second wrapper list.

## Validation
| | `origin/main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| **Live** `hermes chat -q` (xAI grok-4.20), model runs `find <dir> -name '*.tmp' -exec nice rm {} \;` | 3 files deleted, tool row `{"output": "", "exit_code": 0}` | `BLOCKED: Command flagged as dangerous (find -exec/-execdir rm) but single-query mode (-q) runs without a user present…`, files intact |
| Control: bare `-exec rm {} \;` | blocked | blocked (unchanged) |
| `tests/tools/test_approval_find_exec.py` (1 invariant test) | red (`find . -exec sudo rm '{}' \;` not flagged) | green |
| `tests/tools/test_approval*.py` + 10 detection suites (hardline, execution-flag, shell-bypass, gnu-abbrev, command_guards, yolo…) | | 6
title: find -exec behind sudo/env/nice/timeout no longer deletes matches without approval (inspired by Muse Code)

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes update` on the stable channel aborts with "Could not resolve the stable source channel: Command '['git', 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', ...]' timed out after 10 seconds. No update was applied." on every attempt, so the install can never update itself again (a fresh install works because it never runs the probe).

Root cause: the forward-only check in `_head_containing` runs `git merge-base --is-ancestor <release commit> HEAD` with a 10s timeout. When the checkout does not have the release commit as an object, a git older than 2.44 ignores `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` (the variable only exists since 2.44; Ubuntu 24.04 ships 2.43), so the "read-only" probe starts a promisor history download that outlives the timeout. The `TimeoutExpired` then propagates out of `resolve_source_target` and aborts the whole update instead of being treated as "no verdict".

Fix: a timed-out probe returns no verdict and falls through to the GitHub compare API `_head_containing` already uses for shallow checkouts and other inconclusive local answers:

- compare says `behind`/`diverged` → HEAD is not past the release → the normal update path proceeds (its apply stage fetches the release commit itself), so the user updates successfully;
- `ahead`/unreachable → conservatively keep HEAD, exactly the documented "unknown relation keeps HEAD" contract — never moves a checkout backward on a guess.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138716

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/source_releases.py` — `_head_containing.run` catches `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` and returns `None` (no verdict); every probe result is now None-checked, and a missing merge-base verdict falls through to the existing `_github_compare` fallback instead of aborting the update.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_stable_forward_only_shallow.py` — new `test_hung_merge_base_falls_back_to_compare`: with `merge-base` hanging (TimeoutExpired raised), behind → `None` (update proceeds), ahead/unreachable → keep HEAD.

## How to Test

1. `python -m pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_stable_forward_only_shallow.py -q` — Observed result: 6 passed (5 pre-existing + 1 new).
2. With the fix reverted, the new test fails with the very `TimeoutExpired` the issue reports (`tests/hermes_cli/test_stable_forward_only_shallow.py:65: TimeoutExpired`); with the fix it passes, i.e. the exception no longer escapes `_head_containing`.

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read
title: fix(update): a hung merge-base probe falls back to GitHub instead of aborting

author: djbhindi
body:
`kanban block` is a worker handoff: a recently closed run keeps its worker alive for the terminal reaper's two-minute grace. Operators currently lack a non-archiving command that requests immediate termination and reports whether it succeeded.

The single-query Kanban SIGTERM path also calls `os._exit` after foreground cleanup, bypassing the process registry’s background cleanup. A real `AIAgent`, native signal handler, and native background process reproduced a false successful stop with a surviving child. Explicitly reap registered background jobs, including persisted jobs, before that hard exit.

Add `hermes kanban stop TASK --reason TEXT --json`. It blocks dispatch, reuses the existing fingerprint-aware terminal worker reaper without the handoff grace, and preserves the workspace and run history. A worker whose termination cannot be confirmed retains its run evidence; the command returns `stopped: false`, `pending_runs`, and exit code 1. Repeating stop retries those retained workers. The command stops one card and does not release dependent cards.

The supervisor now uses the existing process-tree terminator before the parent disappears. A worker ignoring SIGTERM previously left its background child alive after SIGKILL. The real-agent regression covers responsive and resistant workers, with ordinary and persisted background jobs.

Validation:
- Supported runner, retries disabled: 16 focused tests passed; three host-specific tests skipped on macOS.
- Broader Kanban run: 519 passed, one failed, 11 skipped across 77 files. The failure, `test_infrastructure_spawn_refusal_never_charges_the_card`, also reproduces on unmodified base `ca069e12` on this macOS host.
- Disposable Linux runtime: resistant worker previously returned `stopped=true` with its child alive; with the tree termination change, worker exit was -9 and the child was gone. This uses a real AIAgent and native registry without inference. The pinned runtime carries an equivalent scoped patch, not the full PR head.
- CLI dispatch/JSON, immediate termination, workspace retention, no re-claim, repeat stop, and unverified worker identity are covered.
- `python scripts/check`: all 12 checks passed.

Still draft: the shared tree terminator is best effort. Stop currently confirms the root's exit, but must also report surviving or unverifiable descendants correctly, including disabled escalation and permission failures. The supervisor fix removes reliance on the worker's signal handler; it does not expla

author: 686f6c61
body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes update` on a checkout that rides its default channel resolves the stable release and then asks git whether this checkout already contains it (`_head_containing`, `hermes_cli/source_releases.py`). That probe runs under a 10-second cap, and the ancestry one's failure was unhandled: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <release> <HEAD>` exceeding the cap raised `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, which `select_apply_target` catches as a channel-resolution failure, so the run stopped:

```
→ Update channel: stable
✗ Could not resolve the stable source channel: Command '['git', 'merge-base', '--is-ancestor', '297552a9…', 'd97007c3…']' timed out after 10 seconds. No update was applied.
```

(#138716, Ubuntu 24.04 / Python 3.14 / 0.22.1. A fresh `install.sh` run works, so the checkout itself is healthy.)

That is the opposite of what the helper documents: an unknown relation keeps HEAD. A 10-second ancestry walk is easy to reach on a real install — the walk itself crosses hundreds of thousands of objects, and on git < 2.44 a partial clone also lazy-fetches the missing ones inside this same probe (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH` only exists from 2.44; Ubuntu 24.04 ships 2.43).

The fix routes both relation probes through one guard: a probe that raises `subprocess.SubprocessError` answers "never answered", which this code already treats as the guess a shallow boundary is — the GitHub compare still gets the last word, and only a proven `behind`/`diverged` moves the checkout. `git rev-parse HEAD` stays a hard probe on purpose: without a HEAD sha there is nothing to keep, and the caller must not read a failed read as proof that HEAD is behind.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138716

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/source_releases.py` — `_head_containing` gains a `relation()` guard around the `merge-base --is-ancestor` and `rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` probes: one that cannot answer is "unknown" (keeps HEAD) instead of an exception escaping into the channel-resolution error path. Docstring updated with the third unknown-relation source.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_stable_forward_only_shallow.py` — `test_ancestry_probe_that_times_out_keeps_head`: a real clone with `subprocess.run` patched to raise `TimeoutExpired` on the `merge-base --is-ancestor` invocation. On `main` it fails with the reporter's traceback; with the fix, HEAD is kept when GitHub is unreachable too, and a proven `behind` v
title: fix(update): treat an ancestry probe that cannot answer as an unknown relation

![Sessions end on the gateway](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aae6a61/yIJ_qoX_lrzqXivIx1lUK_2028KD5e.png)

## What does this PR do?

Under the unified gateway (#106742) the classic CLI and Ink are viewers: the agent, its memory manager and the Relay scope live in the gateway. The end-of-session lifecycle still ran in the client process, or not at all. This PR runs it in the gateway when the last viewer closes the session.

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exit or `/new` in the classic CLI or Ink | memory providers' `on_session_end` never runs (only at idle eviction or `hermes gateway stop`) | runs on the gateway when the last viewer closes |
| `on_session_finalize` / `on_session_reset` | fired in the CLI process (classic CLI) or never (Ink, Desktop); the Relay scope is never closed | fired on the gateway under the owning profile; the Relay scope closes |
| Exit while a turn is queued or running | `ended_at` stays unset | the close is remembered and completed at the drain's next idle point |
| Classic CLI on a gateway session | also fired finalize / `on_session_end` itself | leaves them to the gateway, so they don't run twice or in the wrong process |

## Related Issue

**Fixes tracker items LC-1 and LC-2 in #134889, and LC-6 in part.** This PR uses `Refs` instead of `Fixes` because #134889 tracks every finding from the #106742 testing, and `Fixes` would close the whole tracker on merge.

**Still open, for a follow-up:** the rest of LC-6 (Ctrl+D during a tool call still interrupts the turn instead of detaching; a client killed with `kill -9` leaves the session open until idle eviction, because a dropped connection carries no client surface) and NF4 (deleting a session still leaves the branch child and the 7-day `state_meta` rows).

## What does this PR do?

Under the unified gateway (#106742) the gateway owns every session, but editors' MCP servers and `hermes acp` launch flags were still treated as client-side state the gateway either ignored or pinned and refused to change. author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

`bake_bytecode` sealed every baked `.pyc` as `0o444` before packaging (f6713f2762). Squirrel.Mac's ShipIt removes the quarantine attribute from every file in the `.app` before swapping it and aborts the whole install on any error other than "attribute not present" — and macOS returns `EACCES` for that call on a read-only file whether or not the attribute is set. Result (#138659): a macOS update downloads, restarts, fails three times on `Couldn't remove quarantine attribute from ".../__pycache__/...pyc"`, hits "Too many attempts to install, aborting update", and relaunches on the old version. The 0.21.7 Mac update zip ships 26,381 `.pyc` files without owner write.

This bakes the pycs `0o644` instead. The read-only bit was defense-in-depth against pyc rewrites that the macOS signature would observe, but nothing can rewrite them anyway:

- `unchecked-hash` pycs are trusted without source validation and never rewritten (PEP 552) — the same commit's own rationale;
- the bake already fails closed unless every parseable module has a pyc, so no cache-miss write can target the sealed tree;
- the `__pycache__` dirs were already left writable (in-place rebuilds rmtree them), so file-level write protection was the only vestige.

The reporter verified the mechanism end-to-end against a real installed app's ShipIt: the as-built bundle fails on the same `.pyc`; the same bundle with only `u+w` added installs successfully and `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes. Windows is unaffected (MSIX records no file attributes); on AppImage/MSIX the payload mount is read-only regardless, so the mode is moot there.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138659

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

author: ranchhandrobotics
body:
# fix(local-runtime): account for Windows AMD iGPU memory reservations

## What does this PR do?

Fixes managed local-model admission on Windows AMD APUs with a large BIOS-reserved GPU memory pool, such as Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S systems configured with 128 GiB physical RAM and 96 GiB reserved for the GPU.

### Problem

Windows exposes only the remaining approximately 32 GiB as OS physical RAM.
Hermes currently caps every integrated GPU's pool at that OS-visible total:

```python
pool = min(ram_total, _windows_igpu_bytes(device) or ram_total)
```

This is appropriate for an ordinary shared-memory iGPU, but discards the separate GPU reservation on these machines. After headroom, Hermes budgets approximately 25.4 GiB instead of recognizing the reserved memory. A model
that loads successfully with the same llama.cpp Vulkan engine is rejected by the planner and omitted from the router's generated presets. Selecting it then produces HTTP 400, `model '...' not found`, even though its GGUF shards are present.

The affected Windows host also returns two identical Radeon adapter records from DXGI. The existing single-candidate check treats those records as ambiguous and cannot use the adapter's memory figures.

### Solution

- Reuse the existing DXGI adapter probe and deduplicate identical adapter records before selection; do not add another registry/WMI probe.
- Add a Windows-only reservation path when the engine positively identifies an integrated GPU, its name matches the selected AMD adapter, and dedicated memory is at least 75% of OS-visible RAM. Reuse the existing large-pool threshold rather than special-casing a product name or a 96-GiB capacity.
- Account for DXGI dedicated memory plus the shared allowance capped at OS-visible RAM. Apply the existing dedicated-memory margin and UMA headroom to their respective portions.
- Preserve `uma=True`, `ram_available_bytes=0`, and `lazy_reads=False`. Shared RAM is not added again as spill space, and AMD integrated-GPU tensor-loading behavior remains unchanged.
- Use a fresh engine memory reading for live/launch budgets. Subtract aggregate heap occupancy, allowing credit for the outgoing server's `own_bytes`, cap shared availability at currently available OS RAM, retain launch headroom, and never exceed the capacity grant.
- Keep the existing budgeting paths for ordinary small-reservation iGPUs, CPU inference, NVIDIA, discrete GPUs, and supported or ambiguous reservation probes.

The Vulkan heap total is used
title: fix(local-runtime): account for Windows AMD iGPU memory reservations

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

Stops PM from wiping the bundled tools-python's `site-packages` on every digest drift.

Root cause of #138689: the python entry's `site-packages` is a **mutable layer** — a desktop bundle preinstalls its gateway deps there (yaml, spacy, numpy, …), and users `pip install` into it afterwards. But `tree_digest()` counted those bytes into the entry's integrity digest, so the first explicit check after a pip install (`hermes pm install`, the update's `ensure_tools_for_sync`, `pm doctor` remediation, any `ensure("uv")` — uv's closure includes python) saw drift, judged the entry missing, and re-realized it from the **bare upstream `python-build-standalone` install_only archive** — whose `site-packages` is empty. That single "repair" destroyed both layers, which is exactly the reported `site-packages → 0 entries` after every app launch (the `installs/<hash>/environments/*/venv` layer survives because the venv sync never touches the tools store).

The fix gives `tree_digest()` per-package skip dirs with the same runtime-state contract `__pycache__` already has: `Python.digest_skip_dirs = ("site-packages",)`. Facts record the skip spelling, verification treats drift in a mutable layer as runtime state instead of damage to repair away (its integrity stays with `verify()`), and `pm doctor` reports it softly (`?`) instead of steering the user into the destructive repair. For a bundled python entry the "repair" could never restore the right bytes anyway — the correct tree is the bundle build product, not the upstream archive.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138689

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `pm/store.py` — `tree_digest()` takes `skip_dirs` (directory names skipped like `__pycache__`, not descended).
- `pm/package.py` — `Package.digest_skip_dirs` declaration (default empty = every existing package unchanged).
- `pm/packages.py` — `Python.digest_skip_dirs = ("site-packages",)`.
- `pm/install.py` — `_entry_verified()` never fails a skip-dir package on digest drift (verify() still gates); `facts.record` and `_copy_verified_source` use/accept the skip spelling.
- `pm/cli.py` — `pm doctor` reports mutable-layer drift as `?` (not a failing `✗` that invites the destructive reinstall).

## What does this PR do?

The interactive classic CLI loses a switched-to session: `/sessions <n>` (or `/resume <id>`) as the
first action in a fresh CLI, then a prompt, is refused with `permission_denied`, surfaced as

issues that resume, and the switch reaches it only through the agent's `session_id` setter
(`hermes_cli/gateway_agent.py:220-231`). `_sync_agent_to_session`
(`hermes_cli/cli_commands_mixin.py:240`) returns early while no agent exists (`:244-245`), and the
agent is built lazily on the first turn, so a switch made before that turn subscribes nothing while
`_handle_resume_command` (`:977`) commits the local switch at `:1017`. `reopen_session` in the same
block is a no-op on the gateway seam (`hermes_cli/gateway_session_store.py:38-42`, served by

and its siblings `/new` and `/branch` were fixed the same night (`591deb0ae1`, `e6407704c4`,
`611233b178`); the pre-first-turn `/resume` path was never wired. The same refusal class had been
fixed once before for the branch child in `cfaa45ee25` ("subscribe the child in the mutate handler
so the first input is admitted, matching session.create").

Fix: open the switched-to session on this viewer before the switch commits, so the first turn is
admitted. Only an ownership refusal stops the switch (`permission_denied`, `profile_mismatch`),
reported with the existing `resume.switch_failed` copy the gateway shares and every catalog already
translates, naming the session it stayed on. A transient or ownership-free answer (`session_busy`,
`runtime_coordination_required`, `storage_unavailable`, `unknown_execution`, `admission_conflict`,
`not_found`) and a transport failure (unavailable, disconnected, timeout) both proceed, because the
switch's reads are local by design and a turn reports what is left. The already-on branch opens the

## What does this PR do?

Persist automatic dependency-repair attempts before the PM import and build. A SIGKILL during repair previously bypassed the exception-only counter, so every launch could repeat the failed build without reaching the retry limit.

Counting still happens after the kernel lock, live-owner and budget checks. The exception handler counts only an attempt not already recorded; successful repair clears the markers, and explicit repair remains available after the automatic budget is exhausted.

## Related Issue

Addresses #123860, specifically retry accounting. This does not make Android builds survive a session kill or fix the report's other Termux build problems.

Earlier unmerged #124320 identified the same gap. This version also protects the failed-PM-import case raised in its discussion by counting before `from pm.recovery import repair_dependencies`.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/_early_recovery.py` — count automatic attempts before PM import and repair, avoiding a second increment in the normal exception handler.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_early_recovery.py` — run genuinely SIGKILLed children through the retry limit; cover explicit recovery, PM import failure, permission-error counting and lock release.

## How to Test

`HERMES_PYTHON=<PM-built test interpreter> scripts/run_tests.sh tests/hermes_cli/test_early_recovery.py tests/hermes_cli/test_checkout_mutation_guards.py tests/pm/test_takeover_preparation.py tests/pm/test_cold_runtime_e2e.py tests/pm/test_install_state_permissions.py --file-retries 0 -j 2`

Result on macOS/Python 3.14.7: **50 passed, 3 skipped** (Linux-only cases). Ruff on both changed files and `python scripts/check` pass; the latter reports 12 checks.

## Evidence

author: phrac
body:
## Why

When a Hermes run works in a Matrix room, clients only ever see the final reply. Everything between "user sent a message" and "answer arrived" is *inferred* by the client: a typing notification, an ad-hoc 👀 reaction, an edited "working…" bubble with no structure. There is no way for a Matrix client (or a mobile push layer) to render "working on step 3 of 5", "waiting for your exec approval", or "finished, $0.04 spent" — or to show an approval prompt as buttons tied to the run it holds up.

This series makes run state **reported** instead of inferred, as structured data on the messages the gateway already sends. The wire format uses the unstable prefix `org.fluxchat.agent` and is being proposed to the Matrix spec forum as an MSC (matrix-org/matrix-spec-proposals; the MSC PR references this one).

All new behavior is gated on adapters that declare `AGENT_STATUS` — today only the Matrix adapter. Telegram/Discord/Slack/etc. see no behavior change.

## What

Five commits, two features:

**1–4: agent run-state reporting in the Matrix adapter**
- `gateway/agent_status.py` — the `org.fluxchat.agent` payload builders (`working` / `waiting` / `done` / `failed`, step + step count, progress, model, context share, session spend, one-line result).
- The tool-progress bubble carries `working` state with the latest step and step count (threaded through the progress-edit machinery in `run_turn_progress.py`).
- The final reply carries `done`/`failed` with model, context use, estimated spend, and a one-line result; the adapter edits the status bubble to the same final state.
- Exec-approval prompts (`send_exec_approval`) name the run they hold up (`{"run": <event_id>}`).
- Runs left in flight when the gateway dies are settled on restart (orphan settle), and the settle path targets the *first working bubble*, not the last tracked send — so a client that has been following the run's status message never sees it hang in `working` forever.

**5: session bridge** (`gateway/session_bridge.py`)
- Mirrors local (desktop/TUI/webui) sessions into one Matrix room, thread per session, so the same client can watch and steer local sessions with the same protocol fields. Opt-in via gateway config; owns its own mautrix client using the configured access token.

## Protocol sketch

```json
"org.fluxchat.agent": {
  "v": 1, "run": "$request-event-id", "state": "working",
  "step": "Running the tests", "steps": 3, "progress": 0.6
}
```

Full field table and semantics: the draft MSC / p
title: feat(matrix): report agent run state in the protocol (org.fluxchat.agent) + session bridge

body:
Repos that ship skills in Claude Code's layout (`<root>/.claude/skills/`) now load as project skills in trusted repos, and a skill shipped for several harnesses at once loads once instead of being refused as ambiguous.

Port of [cline/cline#14846](https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/14846) (scan `.claude/skills` in the runtime skill search paths), adapted to `agent/skill_utils.py`.

## Changes
- `PROJECT_SKILLS_SUBDIRS` gains `.claude/skills` after `.hermes/skills` and `.agents/skills`. Same trust gate (`skills.trusted_project_dirs`), same scan quarantine, same project tier. The untrusted-repo banner count and `hermes skills trust` hint pick it up automatically.
- `_candidate_project_skills_dirs`: a symlinked `.claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills` counts as one root, not two.
- `pick_skill_candidate`: provably identical copies (same realpath or same bytes) in different roots of one tier resolve to the first-scanned root. Before, only same-root copies did.
- Docs (`skills.md` Project-Local Skills), config comment and `hermes skills trust` help text list the new dir.

## Why the second change is needed
Repos that support several agents usually ship the same skill in both `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`, as a copy or a per-skill symlink. Adding the dir alone made each of those an "ambiguous same-tier collision". The skill dropped out of `hermes skills list` and the prompt index, and `skill_view` refused it, even though it had loaded fine from `.agents/skills` before. I verified this live with the naive one-line port (table below).

Two *different* skills sharing one name across these dirs are still refused, the same as `.hermes/skills` vs `.agents/skills` today. **Reviewer call:** a repo that already loads `foo` from `.agents/skills` and ships a *divergent* Claude-specific `foo` under `.claude/skills` will see `foo` start refusing as ambiguous. The alternative is to let subdir order (`.hermes > .agents > .claude`) break different-content ties inside the project tier. I kept the existing refusal rule because changing it also changes `.hermes` vs `.agents` behaviour.

## Validation
**Live repro:** real `python -m hermes_cli.main skills list` plus `tools.skills_tool.skill_view` in a trusted scratch git repo (isolated `HERMES_HOME`), with `claude-demo` only in `.claude/skills`, `agents-demo` only in `.agents/skills`, and `both-demo` byte-identical in both.

| Tree | `claude-demo` | `agents-demo` | `both-demo` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `origin/main` | not liste

author: Junnn-2004
body:
## What does this PR do?

On Windows, the Desktop update hand-off can refuse its own claim and exit 2, naming the custodian that it started itself (`Another Hermes update is already running (... process <custodian>)`).

`windows.ps1` moves marker line 1 to a custodian before any update work starts, but it never exports `HERMES_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID`. The custodian is a sibling of the `hermes update` child, never its ancestor, so `UpdateLock._is_partner` can only match the line-4 delegate. That delegate line gets erased by the child itself whenever the tree's dependencies are stale or a tail is owed: `hermes_bootstrap` → `venv_sync.prepare_launch` takes and releases a pre-flight claim in the delegate process, and releasing as the delegate drops the line while the owner lives (A7 rule 5). The relaunched `hermes update` then sees only the custodian and refuses.

This PR exports the marker owner the same way `posix.sh` has since 013e94b38a (#134268): the custodian once it is named, and the hand-off's own pid when it is not. It clears the variable before relaunching the Desktop, mirroring `posix.sh`'s `env -u` on relaunch.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138690

The Windows counterpart of #134268 / #134602.

- [ ] 📝 Documentation update

- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

author: leehaney04-creator
body:
## What

`isHermesProcess()` can never identify a process on Windows, so
`findRunningGatewayProfiles()` returns `[]` there and the "running gateway"
rung of the one-time active-profile detection is dead.

## Why

The probe has three steps and Windows dies on the third:

```js
try {
  const cmdline = fs.readFileSync(`/proc/${pid}/cmdline`, 'utf8')  // ENOENT on Windows
  return cmdline.includes('hermes')
} catch {
  try {
    const out = execSync(`ps -p ${pid} -o args=`)                  // procps rejects -o
    return out.includes('hermes')
  } catch {
    return false                                                   // ← always
  }
}
```

Windows has no `/proc`, and the procps `ps` the app ships rejects the
BSD-style `-o` that macOS accepts:

```
ps: unknown option -- o
Try `ps --help' for more information.
```

Both probes throw, so the function returns `false` for every PID — including a
live gateway. The comment on the first probe ("On macOS / Linux") is accurate:
Windows was never handled here.

The other four `ps -o` call sites in the tree are fine, and this PR does not
touch them: `backend-claim.ts:119` has a PowerShell branch above it,
`update-marker.ts:106-134` guards on `process.platform === 'darwin'`, and
`managed-ssh-update.ts:383` is `sys.platform == 'darwin'`.

## Repro (Windows 11, real host, no stubs)

```
process.kill0     = OK (process is alive)
/proc read        = FAIL ENOENT
ps: unknown option -- o
isHermesProcess   -> false          # expected true
```

Preconditions, all verified on the reporting host:

- `gateway.pid` names the live gateway:
  `{"pid": 13088, "kind": "hermes-gateway", ...}`
- `active-profile.json` does not exist, so the migration path actually runs
- `isHermesProcess(13088)` returns `false`

## Consequence

`findRunningGatewayProfiles()` (`profile-migration.ts:107`) returns `[]`, so
`migrateActiveProfileIfMissingPure` never takes its `running.length > 1`
branch (`profile-migration.ts:284`) and the "Running gateway (gateway.pid with
verified liveness + hermes identity)" priority silently degrades to the
state.db heuristic.

Scope is the one-time `active-profile.json` migration — day-to-day runs are
unaffected. That is why the `ps: unknown option -- o` console line looked
cosmetic; the identity check behind it was not.

## Fix

`process-identity.ts` gains a `win32` branch reading
`Win32_Process.CommandLine` via CIM — the same probe `backend-claim.ts` uses
for start markers — matched case-insensitively because Windows
title: fix(desktop): identify hermes processes on Windows, not just macOS/Linux
