body:
A corrupt `plugins/.install-metadata.json` no longer breaks `hermes plugins list` or the Desktop Plugins hub; only the pin annotations disappear, with a warning.

Port of google-gemini/gemini-cli#29720 (there: one extension with unusable install metadata made every extension fail to load and `extensions list` exit with an error). Hermes runtime loading already tolerates a bad sidecar (`plugins_provenance.read_sidecar_rows`), but the two read-only listing paths did not.

## Changes
- `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd_listing.py::cmd_list`: an unreadable sidecar prints a warning to **stderr** (so `--json`/`--plain` stdout stays parseable) and lists without pin annotations.
- `tui_gateway/methods_tools.py::_plugin_rows`: same degrade + a log warning. This feeds `plugins.manage list`, and `toggle`/`settings` re-read it after writing, so a toggle that had already applied used to come back as an RPC error.
- install / update / remove keep refusing on the corrupt file (fail-closed, unchanged). Matches the existing `try/except PluginOperationError` pattern in `catalog_tool._plugin_rows` and `plugins_cmd_catalog._install_record`.

## Validation

**Live repro** (real processes, scratch `HERMES_HOME` with one user plugin + `{broken` sidecar):

| Surface | origin/main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `hermes plugins list` | traceback, `PluginOperationError: Could not read plugin install metadata` | warning on stderr + `okplug` row |
| `hermes plugins list --json` | traceback | stdout parses, `okplug` listed |
| real `python -m tui_gateway.entry`, `plugins.manage list` | `error 5026 Could not read plugin install metadata` | rows returned |
| same, `plugins.manage toggle okplug` | `error 5026` while config.yaml already had it enabled | `ok: true`, row `status: enabled` |
| `hermes plugins remove okplug` | refuses | still refuses, tree intact |

**Tests:** 2 invariant tests (`test_cmd_list_survives_corrupt_install_metadata`, `test_corrupt_install_metadata_still_lists_but_remove_refuses`), red on origin/main source, green here. `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugins_cmd*.py` + `tests/tui_gateway/test_plugins_manage_*.py` green (test_plugins_cmd.py run with the fake-HOME recipe for the worktree home-I/O guard). `scripts/check --only health` ok, ruff clean.

Root cause: `_read_install_metadata()` raises by design for write paths, and two display-only callers used it without the catch the other read-only callers already have.

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes update` could hang forever at "Fetching updates..." with 0% CPU (#138672): the updater's
main thread was blocked writing the stdin of its `git cat-file --batch` child while the child was
blocked writing blob bodies back into stdout — both pipes full, both processes waiting on each
other, and the `timeout=120` passed alongside never able to fire, because the parent is parked
inside a blocking `write()` syscall, not in the select loop where the timeout is checked.

`read_target_files` (the one place that drives a batched `cat-file`, reached from the pre-move
syntax preflight and the recovery-closure read) fed its request with `input=`. subprocess's POSIX
`input=` path writes `PIPE_BUF`-sized chunks on a possibly-blocking fd, and a write that lands when
the stdin pipe has under 512 bytes free parks the parent exactly like the reporter's `sample`
stack (`os_write → _Py_write_impl → write [blocked]`).

The fix writes the request to a `TemporaryFile` and hands it over as `stdin=`: the kernel feeds
git from the file, the parent never writes the pipe — it only reads — so both the deadlock window
and the stuck-timeout window are gone, whatever the child does with its pipes (lazy blob fetches
on a `blob:none` clone included).

## Related Issue

Fixes #138672

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/update_cmd_commit.py` — `read_target_files` writes the `<ref>:<path>` request to a
  `TemporaryFile` and passes it as `stdin=` instead of `input=`; the parent process only reads.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_update_recovery_closure.py` — shape lock: the batch reader must call
  `run_git` with `stdin=<file containing the exact request>` and no `input=` kwarg (red on main,
  green here); flood test: a stand-in `git` that floods stdout to 256 KiB before draining stdin
  completes with the request intact.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_recovery_closure.py::test_the_batch_reader_feeds_the_request_from_a_file_not_a_pipe -q`
   — Observed result: on unpatched `main` it fails at `assert "input" not in seen` (the parent
   writes the pipe); with this change it passes.
2. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_recovery_closure.py -q`
   — Observed result: the batch-reader tests pass; the pre-existing failures in this file are
   identical with and without this change (environment baseline, verified by stash comparison).
3. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_update_r

body:
## What does this PR do?

Prevent two different plugins from silently replacing each other's native CLI commands through `ctx.register_cli_command()`.

On current main, plugin A can register `modernise`, then plugin B registers the same name and `hermes modernise` silently runs B. The command descriptor is overwritten before argparse sees it, so parser-level collision checks cannot resolve this case.

This change preserves the first registry owner. A foreign registration logs a warning naming the command and both plugin IDs, returns `None`, and creates no handle or replacement lease. The same plugin ID may still replace its own command, including through a new context. Admission and registration remain inside the existing replacement transaction.

The small registration body moves into `hermes_cli/plugins_cli_registration.py` to respect the existing facade's code-health size ratchet; no exemption is added.

## Related work / scope

- #13643 previously proposed duplicate rejection but was closed without merging; its closure concerned CLI wiring, not foreign-owner refusal.
- #130608 / #130607 protect parser attachment against built-ins and failing setup. This is a separate, earlier SDK registry boundary and does not replace that work.
- This does not change slash-command or tool overrides, manifest identity selection, memory-provider CLI conventions, or built-in command collision handling. No new override flag or dependency change.
- Compatibility change: cross-plugin native CLI replacement is no longer silently accepted. Same-owner replacement and cleanup remain supported.

## Type of Change

- [x] Regression tests and documentation

- Owner-aware native CLI registration, keyed by plugin registry ID rather than display name.

The second plugin's unrelated command must still work.
- Preserve the existing generic manager-local out-of-order teardown regression on the slash-command mapping, which still accepts overrides; native CLI refusal and same-owner cleanup receive dedicated coverage.
- Document the native SDK ownership contract in English and zh-Hans.

## What does this PR do?

Adds Search1API to the Nous-approved MCP catalog (`optional-mcps/search1api/manifest.yaml`), so it shows up on the Connectors page and installs with `hermes mcp install search1api`.

Search1API runs an official vendor-hosted remote MCP server at `https://mcp.search1api.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, source: https://github.com/superagents-lab/search1api-mcp). It provides live web search across multiple engines, news, single-page reading (`crawl`), sitemaps, and GitHub / Hacker News trending. Users sign in with OAuth in the browser instead of pasting an API key. We already maintain the `search1api` plugin in `plugin-catalog/`; this entry is the no-key, remote-MCP way to use the same service.

Submitted by the maintainer of the server (SuperAgents, LLC / superagents-lab).

## Related Issue

None.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `optional-mcps/search1api/manifest.yaml`: `transport.type: http` to `https://mcp.search1api.com/mcp`, `auth.type: oauth`, `suggest` keywords/hosts, `post_install` notes. No local process, no install step, no env vars.

## How to Test

1. `hermes mcp install search1api`. The entry installs; the probe reports that OAuth is needed.
2. `hermes mcp login search1api`. Verified on main @ 5575a08: an unauthenticated `initialize` returns 401 with RFC 9728 `resource_metadata`; Hermes discovers `https://clerk.s1.dev` as the authorization server, uses its Client ID Metadata Document (`https://nousresearch.github.io/hermes-agent/docs/oauth/client-metadata.json`), and builds an authorize URL with PKCE S256, `resource=https://mcp.search1api.com/mcp` and `scope=offline_access`. The authorization server accepts it and redirects to the Search1API sign-in page. Dynamic Client Registration is also enabled.

author: arcabotai
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the "uploads alone breach the ceiling" variant of #133999 reported by @clckmedia: when reserved user uploads by themselves exceed the outbound image ceiling, `outbound_image_retire_count` stops batching and rewrites the cached prefix on **every** new tool image.

In that branch `_fits(0)` is false, so `max_retire = total - floor` and the loop can never fit (the uploads are reserved), so it always returns exactly `total - floor`. That count tracks `total`, so each new tool image moves the retirement frontier by one and edits a message inside the cached prefix — the per-image frontier the module docstring says this policy exists to avoid. The reported production turn (51 pasted screenshots, then a 60-call `vision_analyze` loop) paid 19 full-prefix rewrites, ~1.9M cache-write tokens.

**Fix (narrow, policy module only):** in the unsatisfiable-block-ceiling branch, keep the satisfiability floor but retire whole batches toward it (`excess - excess % batch`), so the retire count is a step function again and the frontier moves once per `IMAGE_EVICTION_BATCH` images. Kept tool images stay between `floor` and `floor + batch - 1`. The byte budget still binds: if the held carriers would breach it, the count advances further (down to the floor at most) until they fit. Both outbound passes (`context_compressor.evict_stale_outbound_tool_images` and `anthropic_message_convert._evict_old_screenshots`) call this one function, so they stay in lockstep (#113517).

With 51 uploads, kept tool images per request go `1..10, 3..10, 3..10, …` instead of `1, 2, 3, 3, 3, …` (one rewrite per 8 images instead of one per image).

This is independent of the Option A / B call in #133999 (dimension-gated trigger): uploads are not downscaled, so A alone does not reach this branch, as @clckmedia noted. If maintainers prefer "retire nothing when only reserved uploads breach the soft 20-image threshold", that is a one-line change on top of this; this PR keeps the existing floor semantics and only restores batching.

**Note:** Opened as draft because GitHub refused a non-draft `CreatePullRequest` for arcabotai while 3 ready-for-review PRs are already open (#137658 / #137619 / #137756).

## Related Issue

Part of #133999 (the reserved-uploads variant [reported by @clckmedia](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/133999#issuecomment-6162325754)). Does not implement Option A.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue

author: BlancuzziJ
body:
## Summary

`cron/scheduler_script.py::_resolve_script_path` correctly rejects a job script whose **resolved** path escapes `<HERMES_HOME>/scripts/`. But the error it returned printed only `script_path` — the caller-supplied value. When the escape is a symlink (link inside `scripts/`, target outside it), that value sits *inside* the scripts directory, so the message read:

```
Blocked: script path resolves outside the scripts directory
(/home/hermes/.hermes/scripts): '/home/hermes/.hermes/scripts/anne_bonny_alerts.py'
```

The path named is inside the very folder the message says was escaped. Every naive reading concludes Hermes is wrong about its own directory, and the reporter can neither see the escaping target nor learn what to do about it.

This is not hypothetical: it cost a real user ~32 consecutive hours of an hourly job failing silently, and the message offered no remedial step. The reporter's own words: *"I should not receive errors like this without some remedial suggestion."*

## Change

- When the resolved target differs from the caller's value, print both — `'<given>' -> '<resolved>'` — so the escape is visible. The arrow is only added for absolute inputs, so a plain relative traversal isn't padded with noise.
- State the cause (a symlink pointing out of the folder, or a `..` segment) and the fix: keep the real file in the scripts dir, point the job at a bare filename, and symlink the **other** direction if an outside path must keep working.

No behaviour change — the same paths are accepted and rejected as before; only the failure text is richer. No test currently pins this string, so nothing needed updating.

## Test Plan

Exercised `_resolve_script_path` directly against four real cases:

- **symlink escape** (`scripts/x.py -> /home/hermes/secops/x.py`) → blocked, now shows the arrow and the target
- **traversal** (`../secops/x.py`) → blocked, same verdict plus the added guidance
- `digest_report.py` → **still passes**
- `/home/hermes/.hermes/scripts/digest_report.py` → **still passes**

The two passing cases matter: the guard's containment behaviour is unchanged.

## Notes

Not a security fix — the guard already blocked the path correctly and should keep doing so. This is purely about the failure being diagnosable without reading Hermes internals.
title: fix(cron): show the resolved target and a remedy when a script path escapes the scripts dir

author: lucasgenta
body:
## Problem

A model asked for "no changes" (e.g. a cron/watcher lane instructed to emit NOCHANGE when there is nothing to report) may answer with the bare control token instead of sentence prose. A whole-output `NOCHANGE` then reaches the chat as literal user-visible text — the same class of leak the existing silence markers (`[SILENT]`, `NO_REPLY`, …) already guard against.

## Fix

Add `NOCHANGE` / `[NOCHANGE]` to `LIVE_GATEWAY_SILENT_MARKERS` in `gateway/response_filters.py`. Both the exact interactive rule and the loose autonomous-lane rule pick them up automatically (the autonomous prefix rule derives from the same set, so `[NOCHANGE] nothing to report` suppresses too). Prose that merely mentions the token is still delivered normally — only exact whole-output matches suppress.

## Test evidence

- New `test_nochange_control_token_is_silence_not_chat_text` in `tests/gateway/test_response_filters.py`: exact match for both forms, autonomous-lane prefix form, and a prose negative case.
- Validated the canonicalization + membership logic standalone against the patched file (exact/bracketed/case-folded forms suppress; prose mentioning the token does not). Full pytest suite could not run in this environment (no pytest installed); CI will confirm.
title: fix(gateway): treat whole-output NOCHANGE as a silence marker

## What does this PR do?

Since the unified gateway runtime merge, hosted group rooms never ran member turns: the room driver called the in-process transport's `submit()` without the keyword-only `member_id` argument that `HostedRoomServerRPC.submit()` requires, so the call raised `TypeError` inside the driver — the member never replied and the task stayed `running` with no error logged (#138660).

The same call also conditionally forwarded an `attachments` kwarg that no transport implementation accepts. Bound attachments have no downstream consumer yet — the in-process `prompt.submit` path ignores them and the peer dispatch wire has no field for them (the shared hookups that e87bd098ea notes are "supplied separately to their owners" are still pending) — so that kwarg could only widen the `TypeError` window. It is dropped here until that landing exists.

This restores the exact submit shape that last worked at 6ebd92d:

- declare `member_id: str` on the `InternalSessionRPC.submit` protocol so the contract matches both real transports (`HostedRoomServerRPC` requires it; `PeerHostedRoomTransport` already accepts it)
- pass `member_id=_member_id(task)` at the driver's submit call site
- stop forwarding the premature `attachments` kwarg

## Related Issue

Fixes #138660

The host uses the Render SDK to create paid sandboxes, execute shell commands, transfer files and terminate resources. Development-only test runners reuse existing local CLI logins when explicitly invoked; they are not called by plugin registration or execution.

author: 686f6c61
body:
## What does this PR do?

Restores the member identity on every hosted-room submit, so group member turns run again.

`#106742` (`eb75627`) dropped two things at once: the `member_id` argument in
`HostedRoomRuntime._execute_attempt`'s `transport.submit(...)` call, and the same
parameter from the `InternalSessionRPC` protocol declaration. `HostedRoomServerRPC.submit`
still requires it as a keyword-only argument — one in-process RPC instance serves every
member of the gateway, so the member cannot be inferred from the RPC instance.

Submitting without it raises `TypeError` inside the driver. The driver cannot tell that
boundary failure apart from an ambiguous post-submit observation failure, so it marks the
attempt ambiguous: the member never answers, the room task stays `running`, and nothing in
the log names the cause.

`tui_gateway/hosted_room_driver.py` carried `member_id=_member_id(task)` at `6ebd92d`;
the merge lost it. The peer transport already tolerates the keyword
(`del member_id  # the signed route already names the member`), so the only transport that
needs the value is the in-process one that has always required it. The per-member authority
producer (`gateway/session_hosted_rpc.py`, added after `6ebd92d` by `bd22e0f9c4`) is now
handed the keyword too and ignores it the same way — without that, restoring the argument
would have moved the `TypeError` to the authority path instead of fixing it.

## Follow-up commits

Three maintainer commits were pushed onto this branch (`e4f86bd`, `e644d21`, `048549d`; details in the review). `HostedRoomAuthorityRPC` and `PeerHostedRoomTransport` now refuse a `member_id` that does not match the member they are bound to, and the new tests drive real transports; the sections below are updated to match. The `attachments` half (#138684) is fixed separately in #138743, stacked on this PR.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138660

Regression from the unified gateway runtime merge, listed by @teknium1 in the post-merge
tracker #134889.

## What does this PR do?

The shared gateway runs in its own working directory, and several paths that a local session names were resolved against that directory. This PR resolves them against the session's own folder.

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@file` / `@folder` / `@diff` / `@git` from a local client | expanded against the gateway daemon's folder | expanded against the session's folder, which is also the allowed root |
| `@file` from the classic CLI | expanded twice, by the CLI and then again by the gateway | expanded once, by the gateway |
| Ink path completion | lists the daemon's folder | lists the session's folder (the launch folder before a session exists) |
| Ink image attach with a relative path | resolved against the ui-tui install folder | resolved against the session's folder; for a remote gateway URL, the launch folder |

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes an unrecoverable fail-closed wedge in the bounded hook runner: a `pre_tool_call` worker whose thread never unwinds (its timeout kill did not propagate to `communicate()`) held its abandoned-worker slot forever, so once `_HOOK_MAX_ABANDONED_WORKERS` (3) wedged slots piled up, **every** later tool call failed instantly with `pre_tool_call plugin callback timed out or is still running` until an MCP reload or restart — hours of total tool-execution outage from one slow hook under load (#138644).

The slot bookkeeping now records when each abandoned slot was taken. At the cap, a slot older than `_HOOK_ABANDONED_SLOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS` (600s) is evicted and one replacement worker may start:

- **600s is beyond any legitimate drain** — a shell-hook subprocess times out at ≤300s plus a ~1s drain, so a slot still held at 600s belongs to a wedged thread, not a live straggler.
- **The leak stays bounded** — the existing 60s suppression window still rate-limits replacement starts, so the worst case is one leaked daemon thread per window instead of a permanent full outage.
- **Fail-closed semantics are preserved** — young slots at the cap keep skipping exactly as before; if the replacement also times out, its slot re-fills the cap and fail-closed skips resume immediately.

This is the containment variant of the fix sketched in the issue: it does not change fail-open/closed policy or add config surface, it just removes the "no recovery path short of a restart" failure mode.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138644

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

- `hermes_cli/plugins_dispatch.py` — abandoned slots now record the monotonic time they were taken (`_hook_abandoned` becomes `dict[key, dict[gate_key, float]]`); at the cap the oldest slot is evicted with a loud warning when older than the new `_HOOK_ABANDONED_SLOT_MAX_AGE_SECONDS`; release paths updated for the dict shape (aged-out slots release as a no-op).
- `hermes_cli/plugins.py` — `_hook_abandoned` type annotation updated to the timestamped shape.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_hook_abandoned_slot_aging.py` — new: young slots at the cap still fail closed with no new worker; an aged slot is evicted, admits exactly one replacement, and the replacement's own timeout re-fills the cap.

Kanban stop and provider-recovery nudges assumed the built-in `kanban_*` terminal tool names. A worker whose board lifecycle is supplied by a plugin could be told to call unavailable tools, and the stop guard could fail to recognize a successful plugin hand-off.

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

`hermes plugins install` treats any `package.json` at the plugin root as a Node sidecar and offers to `npm ci` it. Desktop/dashboard plugins that ship a prebuilt bundle keep `package.json` only for their build and test toolchain (esbuild, TypeScript, vitest — all under `devDependencies`). For those plugins the question claims "declares Node dependencies" when there are no runtime dependencies at all, and answering yes installs the entire dev toolchain into the plugin folder. The reporter measured `hermes-cloud-file-manager` v0.4.5 (9 devDependencies, empty `dependencies`): the installer's own command installs 84 packages / 108 MB, all unused at runtime.

This gates the Node consent question on the manifest actually declaring runtime deps (`dependencies` / `optionalDependencies`). A build-only manifest skips the question with a dim explanatory line; nothing is installed for runtime either way, so this cannot break a working sidecar. A `package.json` that fails to parse keeps today's prompt (fail-open) so npm itself surfaces the breakage rather than the installer silently skipping the sidecar.

The update path (`_refresh_declared_dependencies`) is intentionally untouched: it only reinstalls a sidecar the user already accepted (target has `node_modules`) and its package.json/lockfile moved, so changing it would drop deps the user explicitly consented to.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138640

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/plugins_cmd_install.py`: added `_node_sidecar_declares_runtime_deps()` — parses the plugin's `package.json` and reports whether `dependencies`/`optionalDependencies` declare anything; unreadable JSON fails open to `True`. `_install_plugin_python_deps()` now asks the Node question only when runtime deps are declared, and prints a dim "build toolchain only" skip line otherwise.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_plugin_dependency_consent.py`: `test_node_sidecar_question_stays_independent` now uses a `package.json` with a real runtime dependency (its `'{}'` fixture would now correctly skip the question, changing what the test exercises). Added `test_build_only_package_json_skips_the_node_question` (devDependencies-only manifest on a TTY: no prompt, no npm install) and `test_unreadable_package_json_keeps_the_node_question` (invalid JSON still prompts and installs).

author: oddepic
body:
## Bug Description

Retrying a failed turn in Desktop (the Retry button on the error card) resubmits the prompt as a brand-new turn, so every click appends another copy of the user message. The copies stay in the transcript even after a later retry succeeds.

## Root Cause

`planReload` / `planRestore` / `planEdit` (`apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-prompt-actions/rewind.ts`) treat every failed turn as never having reached the gateway (#86573 / #86623) and send no truncation address. That holds for admission failures, but a provider failure lands after the user row is stored, so the plain resubmit duplicates it. The backend only merges adjacent user rows and the failure notice sits between the copies, so nothing collapses them.

## Fix

- When the failed turn's user row carries a durable row id, rewind to it (`truncate_before_row_id`, no ordinal, so the #86573 ordinal mis-aim cannot happen). The plain resubmit stays only for turns that never persisted (#86623).
- A row-id rewind that would archive later user turns goes through the deep-cut confirm (#133716); a tail retry still sends on the first click.
- Same change in all three planners (reload, restore, edit), which both the primary chat and session tiles share.

## How to Verify

1. In Desktop, send a prompt while the provider fails (e.g. an invalid API key).
2. Click Retry: the transcript keeps one user bubble and one failure notice, no duplicate.
3. Fix the provider and click Retry again: one user bubble, one reply.

## Test Plan

- [x] Added regression tests for this bug (5 in `rewind.test.ts`, proven red on the base commit)
- [x] Existing tests still pass (`rewind`, `session-tile-actions`, `use-prompt-actions` index/deep-cut, thread suites: 245 tests)
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` clean on the changed files
- [ ] Manual verification of the fix
- [ ] CI green

## Risk Assessment

Low. The only behavior change is Desktop retry/edit/restore of a failed turn that already has a durable row id, and the cut goes through the existing guarded rewind path (`confirm_truncate`, row-id resolution that fails closed, soft-archived rows). Turns with no row id resubmit exactly as before.
title: fix(desktop): rewind persisted failed turns on retry instead of duplicating them

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_preflight()` in the WhatsApp adapter only checked that `creds.json` **exists**. When the Node bridge process is killed mid-write (crash, restart, power loss), Baileys can leave `creds.json` truncated to 0 bytes — that file still passes the existence check, so the gateway assumes the session is paired and launches the bridge headless. The bridge cannot authenticate with empty creds, dumps QR codes into `bridge.log`, and every dispatch burns the full 30s connect budget before failing with `HTTP 503: Not connected to WhatsApp` (#138627).

This adds a `_has_valid_creds()` check: creds.json must be a plausible paired Baileys credential file (≥100 bytes, parseable JSON object, containing `noiseKey` and `signedIdentityKey`). A file that exists but fails validation now fails fast with a distinct non-retryable `whatsapp_creds_invalid` fatal error pointing at re-pairing, instead of the headless QR/timeout loop. A merely *missing* file keeps the existing `whatsapp_not_paired` error.

The key-shape requirement also catches a half-finished pairing state (valid JSON with only `registrationId`/`advSecretKey`), which equally cannot authenticate headless.

- `tests/gateway/test_whatsapp_creds_preflight.py` (new): unit coverage for the validator (0-byte, truncated JSON, half-paired JSON, wrong-shape JSON, valid creds, missing file) plus `_preflight` integration asserting the named fatal error per state.

body:
## What does this PR do?

Under a multiplexed Desktop backend, a served profile whose `config.yaml` has no `mcp_servers` key of its own silently gets zero MCP tools: `start_background_mcp_discovery()`'s config gate bare-returns, so no discovery pass ever runs for that profile and the live shared connections of the launch home never reach it — with no log line in the profile's own log (#138622). Worse, the home was added to `_mcp_discovery_started` *before* the gate, so the next agent build entered the retry branch and logged a bogus `"Background MCP discovery previously exited with no connected servers; retrying discovery thread"` warning for a thread that never ran and would never be retried.

This PR makes the gate observable and stops polluting the started set:

- When the gate skips, log **once per home** (not per build): a `warning` when other profile homes in this backend already ran discovery — the multiplex case, pointing at the invisible shared servers — and an `info` line otherwise, so single-profile setups without MCP don't get warning noise.
- The home is no longer marked started on the skip path, so the bogus retry warning is gone and a later `hermes mcp add` starts discovery through the normal path.

The full "adopt shared servers with no config of one's own" direction from the issue is deliberately not attempted here: discovery is config-driven and `reconcile_mcp_servers_with_config()` tears down servers missing from the owning config, so a no-config adopt needs cross-scope semantics that don't fit a focused fix. The reporter's verified workaround (mirror the `mcp_servers` entry into the served profile's config) keeps working, and after this PR the skip is diagnosable in minutes from that profile's own log.

## What does this PR do?

Adds Azure AD / Entra certificate client-credentials (`client_assertion`) to the Microsoft Teams platform connector, as an alternative to `TEAMS_CLIENT_SECRET`.

body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the four restart-and-recovery problems found while testing the unified gateway (#106742), now on `main`. Before this change, a `hermes gateway restart` could leave no gateway running at all. The classic CLI never re-attached afterwards. Queued API callers were told to retry work that would run anyway. After a crash, every local client hung while the database check ran.

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hermes gateway restart` on a manual or client-started gateway | SIGUSR1, waits for a supervisor relaunch that never comes, exits 1, **no gateway running**; cron and bots stay down | stops the gateway, drops the cached host-gateway probe, and starts a new one |
| Interactive classic CLI after the gateway restarts | every prompt fails with "The model request failed. Run /model to switch..." until the CLI is restarted | the next gateway call reconnects and resumes the open sessions: prompts, `/resume`, `/branch`, `/handoff`, `/bg`, `/btw`, `/stop`, the dock and `/new` all work; `/bg` never falls back to an in-process agent |
| A turn running when the gateway goes away | reported as a model failure | reported as a lost gateway connection with an unknown outcome (never resent) |
| `chat -q` whose turn the restart drain interrupted | exits 130 silently | exits 130 and says the turn was interrupted and why |
| API caller queued behind a running turn when the gateway restarts | `503 runtime_draining` + `Retry-After: 1`; the row still runs once, so a retrying client (the OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs by default) **submits twice**; `/v1/runs` reports `run.failed` | `503 admission_queued`, message "your input is saved ... do not resend it", `x-should-retry: false`, no `Retry-After`; `/v1/runs` reports `queued` |
| Local clients after an unclean exit | hang for the whole `state.db` `quick_check` (41-76 s on 5.3 GB, 7m43s reported on 6.3 GB) | served at once; on a WAL store the check runs in a background thread with a 1800 s deadline; on a rollback-journal store it is skipped with one warning, because a long scan there would block live writes |

author: ruizanthony
body:
> Draft because GitHub rejects ready-for-review / non-draft creation for this account (#131859); local validation complete.

## What does this PR do?

A one-shot `hermes chat -q/-Q` run keeps `notify_on_complete`, but once the turn ends it lingers for those processes only within **one** budget, `terminal.oneshot_completion_wait_seconds` (600 s by default). The quiet drain loop and the exit linger share that budget (`hermes_cli/quiet_single_query.py`, `hermes_cli/cli_shutdown.py`). The background spawn result says nothing about this bound. An agent can therefore launch a 15-minute test suite with `notify_on_complete=true` and end its turn expecting to be woken. The run exits after the budget and the work is left without an owner.

We hit this in production with agent-run deliveries launched as `hermes chat --resume <id> --query-file <brief> -Q`. The owner agent started a validation in the background with notify, then ended its turn. The process exited exactly 600 s later while the validation was still running, and nobody received the completion. Three such stops happened in three weeks; one blocked a release queue for several hours.

When a single-query session (`HERMES_SINGLE_QUERY_SESSION=1`) keeps `notify_on_complete`, the spawn result now carries an `oneshot_note`. The note gives the real bound read from config, or says the run will not wait at all when the linger is disabled (`<= 0`). It also tells the agent to wait for the process itself with `process(action='wait')`.

This only adds an informational field; no behavior changes:
- interactive sessions get no note;
- stateless one-shots (`hermes -z`, API server, Kanban workers) keep `notify_unsupported` only;
- subagents keep `subagent_note` only;
- spawns without notify are unchanged.

## Related Issue

No existing issue found. Searched open/closed PRs for "oneshot completion", "oneshot_completion_wait_seconds" and "notify_on_complete single query". Related context: #92861 (one-shot linger for notify processes), #114898 (bot-chat delivery and the 600 s linger).

author: liuhao1024
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the silent discovery failure reported in #138601: `tool_search` never surfaced a connected hosted connector's tools when the query contained natural domain words.

Root cause: the gateway connector leg already ranks relevance for the whole use_case, but `dispatch_tool_search` merged those entries into the local corpus and re-ran the rarest-token gate over them. A domain word no catalog document carries ("zones", "dns", "workers") has maximal IDF, became the gate token, and rejected every gateway entry — so `matches` came back empty. Because the gateway leg itself succeeded (`hosted_failure: None`), no unavailable hint was attached either, and `available_sources` never listed connectors, so the model had no signal that the capability existed and concluded the app was unsupported.

The fix, contained to the dispatch layer (the `search_catalog` gate semantics for local tools are untouched):

- Search the gateway's per-query shortlist separately; when the lexical pass over that shortlist is empty, keep the entries in gateway order instead of dropping them (the gateway already judged them relevant to the use_case).
- Include connected connectors in `available_sources`, so an empty result group names what is connected and the existing retry hint becomes actionable.
- Normalize the entry `source_name` to the lowercase connector slug the composed tool name is already built from, so vendor-cased gateway schemas don't leak mixed-case source rows.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138601

## Type of Change

author: ydmw74
body:
## Summary

Native adapter shims (`CodexAuxiliaryClient` / `AsyncCodexAuxiliaryClient` — the `openai-codex` OAuth and xAI Grok OAuth auxiliary routes) translate chat-completions kwargs into their native protocol **inside** the provider callback, so Relay only ever sees the chat-shaped request body. The Rust `OpenAIResponsesCodec` requires the Responses `input` field and fails decode **before** the callback runs:

```
invalid argument: OpenAI Responses request is missing input
```

This killed every `openai-codex` MoA reference slot on each fan-out: the slot reported `[failed: invalid argument: OpenAI Responses request is missing input]` and the turn silently degraded to fewer references (observed 18/18 failures on `openai-codex` slots, 0 on anthropic slots in the same preset, from `agent/relay_llm.py:880` — `MoA reference model openai-codex:<model> failed: ...`).

## Fix

Map the shim clients to the **chat codec** at every Relay choke point (sync, async, streaming) and in the route-context fallback, via the new `_relay_visible_aux_api_mode()` helper — Relay decodes what it actually sees (the chat-shaped body). The shim keeps owning the real Responses wire. Raw OpenAI SDK clients on a Responses endpoint keep the Responses codec unchanged — their body really is Responses-shaped.

## Verification

- Standalone reproduction with the installed `nemo_relay` package: `OpenAIResponsesCodec.decode()` on a chat-shaped body raises exactly this RuntimeError; `OpenAIChatCodec` decodes it fine.
- A/B on a live profile: before the fix every `openai-codex` MoA reference failed with the missing-input error; after the fix both reference slots (anthropic + openai-codex) complete.
- New regression test `test_codex_shim_relay_uses_chat_codec_not_responses` drives the **real** managed relay pipeline end-to-end with a `CodexAuxiliaryClient`-shaped shim and `api_mode=codex_responses`: fails with the missing-input RuntimeError before the fix, completes after.
- `tests/agent/test_auxiliary_relay.py` 13/13 green; 69 related MoA/aux tests green (2 pre-existing failures unrelated, fail identically without this change).
title: fix(relay): decode Codex shim aux calls with the chat codec, not the Responses codec

body:
<!-- hermes-draft-gate -->

> creation and draft→ready for external authors). The fix is complete and tested —
> please treat it as ready for review / salvage.

## What does this PR do?

When Bedrock sends an exception frame mid-stream, the Anthropic SDK's Bedrock event-stream decoder raises a bare

```
ValueError("Bad response code, expected 200: {'status_code': 400, 'headers': {':exception-type': 'internalServerException', ...}, 'body': b'{"message":"The system encountered an unexpected error during processing. Try your request again."}'}")
```

`classify_api_error` rates this `FailoverReason.unknown` / `retryable=True`, but `agent/turn_api_error.py::_is_local_validation_error` treats every `ValueError` as a local programming bug. `settle_unrecovered_error` therefore sets `is_client_error=True`, logs `Non-retryable client error` after attempt 1/3, and ends the turn with no output — even though Bedrock itself says to retry. `api_max_retries`, `auto_recovery_cycles` and the classification hook can't change that, because the local-validation verdict overrides them.

The fix exempts the decoder's transient exception frames from the local-validation verdict, exactly like the existing exemption for jiter stream-parse `ValueError`s (#65147), so they go through the normal 5xx-style retry/backoff. Only Bedrock's transient types are exempted; a `validationException` frame is a genuine client error and keeps the non-retryable path.

This re-implements @rayjun's #44054 onto the current structure: that PR patched the inline classifier in `agent/conversation_loop.py`, which has since moved into `agent/turn_api_error.py`, so it no longer applies (CONFLICTING since). See Credits.

author: tmaarcxs
body:
## What

`agent/kanban_stop.py::session_called_kanban_terminal()` keeps score of worker ownership by scanning the transcript for terminal kanban tool **names** (`kanban_complete`, `kanban_block`, `kanban_schedule`, `kanban_request_review`, `kanban_request_changes`), never their **outcomes**. A handler rejection (structured `tool_error` JSON) leaves the call and its `role:"tool"` result row in the transcript, so the guard reported "already handed off" and returned `None` for the rest of the session — the corrective nudge went permanently silent after a single rejected handoff, and the next narrated stop exited `rc=0` with the card still `running` as a `protocol_violation` (#136843). This PR reads each terminal result row's outcome instead:

- a rejection suppresses only its own call id, so a later retried attempt is judged on its own outcome (a rejection followed by a successful retry stays terminal);
- rejections are recognized in the two shapes they actually take: the handler's structured `{"error": ...}` JSON — including the common variant where a harness notice (`[Tool loop warning: ...]`) is appended after the JSON body, which defeats a whole-string `json.loads` — and the executor's plain `Error executing tool '...'` failure string (e.g. a tool timeout);
- successful `{"ok": ...}` payloads, duplicate-result placeholders, empty and unparseable rows still count as landed (fail-open), so the guard cannot nag a worker that genuinely handed the card off.

The core `turn_stop_gates` call path is unchanged: the gate then nudges the worker to retry the lifecycle call instead of exiting silently.

## Why this shape

The suppression is keyed by `tool_call_id` rather than a session-wide flag because the transcript is append-only history: a call rejected at turn 12 and retried successfully at turn 14 must read as terminal, and the reverse ordering must too. Fail-open on unrecognized shapes keeps the blast radius at zero for workers whose transcript rows don't match the canonical handler payloads.

## Evidence (live worker session DB, 2,334 sessions touching a terminal tool)

- 5,661 persisted terminal-tool rows replayed through the new row classifier: every row agrees with its independently parsed ground truth (2,406 ok payloads, 771 structured rejections, 1,911 rejection rows carrying an appended harness notice, 1 executor timeout string, 548 duplicate placeholders).
- Full-session replay: the guard verdict changes for exactly 32 sessions — old logic said "handed
title: fix(agent): keep the kanban stop nudge after a REJECTED terminal call

body:
## What does this PR do?

**Packaging/root-cause slice of #136707.** On the official Docker image the holographic memory provider runs **silently FTS-only** because the sealed environment ships without NumPy, and an offline/immutable container cannot lazy-install the plugin's dependencies into `/opt/data/installs`. Without NumPy, `FactRetriever` redistributes `hrr_weight` 0.3 → 0.0, so `probe`/`related`/`reason`/`contradict` lose HRR structural recall and new facts store no vectors — with green logs everywhere.

The plugin already declares `numpy>=1.26,<3`, but that only helps when plugin dependencies can be installed on demand. This PR bakes NumPy into the **image** for users who can't do that, following the existing `matrix` / `google-chat` precedent ("providers Docker users can't lazy-install in a sealed container").

Changes:
- **`pyproject.toml`:** new small `holographic` extra pinning `numpy==2.4.3` (the exact pin `voice`/`wake` already use → one-version contract), deliberately **not** in `[all]` (opt-in-backend policy).
- **`pm/extras.py`:** `"holographic": "numpy"` anchor for fast, resolver-free availability checks.
- **`Dockerfile`:** bake `--extra holographic` into the sealed, selection-recorded venv, so HRR works out of the box including air-gapped containers (and the recorded baseline keeps it across stage2 refreshes).
- **`uv.lock`:** refreshed with the repo-pinned uv 0.12.3 — membership-only, 6-line diff.
- **docs:** "NumPy, HRR, and Docker" — why `PYTHONPATH` cannot inject NumPy (the launcher clears it), the `.pth` bind-mount escape hatch, and same-text `update_fact` re-vectorization for rows stored with `hrr_vector = NULL`.
- **tests:** a static, no-Daemon packaging contract so the bake is enforced on every machine / in CI without building the image.

## What does this PR do?

Fixes the P0 restart-loop root cause from #138343 part 1 (and the same class in #133744): a leftover host rendezvous record whose recorded pid is no longer the publisher must not vouch for that host forever.

Every live publisher holds `host-gateway.lock` for its lifetime and the OS releases that flock on death. This PR makes that lock the ownership proof it was always meant to be, at the shared liveness/attach boundary, instead of trusting process-incarnation heuristics alone.

## Related Issue

Addresses #138343 part 1 (gateway restart loop after unclean death + recycled pid). Parts 2 and 3 of that issue are separate workstreams (#138348, #138484).

Related, non-duplicate work:
- #138342 bounds the transient refuse only for records with **no** incarnation proof, after a 90s attach-path grace. It does not change `liveness_is_proven`, does not probe the host lock, and cannot reach records that *carry* `createTime`/`startTime` (the reboot tick-collision family of #133744).
- #133750 adds `bootEpoch` + cmdline checks inside `_record_incarnation_matches`. Complementary: it hardens the incarnation proof itself; this PR proves ownership from the flock and refuses records with no incarnation fields at all.
- #118726 consults `gateway_state.json` when the socket cannot answer, for a different symptom (standalone misread as multiplexer).

Request `tree_format: "elements"` for AX/SOM window captures only when the live input schema accepts it. Cua >= 0.35 defaults to compact Markdown, which omits the structured elements, frames and per-element tokens Hermes already consumes. author: kshitijk4poor
body:
## What this fixes

After a reboot, a supervised `hermes gateway run` can exit 75 in a loop forever and never start. The dead gateway's host record names a low PID that an unrelated early-boot process now holds. Boot-relative `/proc` start ticks reset on reboot, so the reused PID lands inside `START_TIME_DRIFT_TOLERANCE`. Liveness looks proven, the control socket never answers, and `decide()` refuses (transient) every time.

Fixes #133744. Salvages #138565 (@ethernet8023), which salvaged #133750 (@sin5ddd). Targets `release/0.22.1`.

## Changes

- **@sin5ddd (#133750, two commits, authorship kept):** new records publish `bootEpoch` (boot id + PID 1 start); a mismatch is a different incarnation. An empty epoch never stales a live owner. The argv-substring identity check was removed in review.
- **@ethernet8023 (#138565, two commits, authorship kept):**
  - A legacy gateway record (no epoch) dated before this boot is judged by the host lock: a live gateway holds it, a dead one's flock is released by the OS. This keeps a running owner live through a forward clock step (#117505).
  - A record with neither `createTime` nor `startTime` never vouches for a PID (#138342 shape).
- **Follow-up (this PR):** the lock probe no longer creates the lock dir or file from read-only callers (status, dashboard, topology). A missing lock file means nobody holds the lock, and the probe reuses `gateway.status._probe_lock_file`. Also: docstring corrected (an empty epoch is not a no-op, because every non-`/proc` record takes the lock path), a dead `getattr` guard dropped, and the reboot test now asserts that no lock file is created.

## Verification (Linux)

Each record below names a live process; every tree was run with its own interpreter.

| record | release/0.22.1 | #133750 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| previous-boot legacy record, PID reused by another process (the wedge) | live (wedge) | stale | stale |
| no createTime, no startTime, reused PID | live (wedge) | live (wedge) | stale |
| foreign `bootEpoch` | live | stale | stale |
| live legacy owner, createTime 600s off the live reading (#117505) | live | stale | live |
| live owner holding the host lock, createTime before boot (clock step) | live | stale | live |
| after the check, can a new claim take the lock while the owner lives? | no | no | no |
| lock dir created by a read-only staleness check | no | no | no |

- **Targeted suite:** the 19 test files that touch host rendezvous and host attach. 9 failures, identical
title: fix(gateway): a recycled PID after reboot no longer wedges the supervised gateway (#133744, salvage #138565)

author: danyim
body:
## What happens

`redact_registered_vault_values()` — the catch-all that scrubs a secret echoed back into tool output —
does a plain substring replace over every value the vault-fill path registers:

```python
for value in values:
    if value in text:
        text = text.replace(value, "«redacted-vault-secret»")
```

Short registered values are normal: a 3-digit CVC, a 5-character expiry like `12/27`, a 4-digit CID.
So the replace hits innocent data. Reproduced on `main`:

```python
register_vault_redaction_value("12")
redact_registered_vault_values("12/10/2024 - 12/12/2025")
#  '«redacted-vault-secret»/10/2024 - «redacted-vault-secret»/«redacted-vault-secret»/2025'
```

```python
register_vault_redaction_value("100")
redact_registered_vault_values("Business Platinum Card (-21008)")
#  'Business Platinum Card (-2«redacted-vault-secret»8)'
redact_registered_vault_values("total 1,100.50")
#  'total 1,«redacted-vault-secret».50'
```

The impact is on the model's view of tool output (not a leak, which is why it is easy to miss): dates
lose a month, account numbers lose digits, amounts lose hundreds. Anything reasoning over dates or card
identifiers — a statement/ledger workflow, for instance — silently reads corrupted values, and a
redacted month is indistinguishable from a genuinely absent one.

## Fix

Two guards, keeping the protection intact:

1. **Never redact inside a date or time token** — `\b\d{1,4}[/-]\d{1,2}[/-]\d{1,4}\b` and
   `\b\d{1,2}:\d{2}(?::\d{2})?\b` are located first, and a match inside one is returned unchanged.
2. **Anchor short values at delimiters** — for a value shorter than `_VAULT_REDACTION_SHORT_MAX` (6),
   require a delimiter on both sides that is not a word character and not one of the separators that
   live inside numbers and dates (`, . / -`). A standalone `100` is still masked; the `100` in `21008`
   or `1,100.50` is not.

Values of 6+ characters keep verbatim substring replacement, unchanged — a long secret embedded in a
larger token must still be caught. Matching is done in a single alternation regex (values remain sorted
longest-first, so a substring can never shadow its superstring) with one replacer that consults the
date/time spans.

## Verification

New `tests/agent/test_vault_value_redaction_boundaries.py` — 6 cases: a month inside a date, an expiry
fragment inside a full date, a masked-account-number, an amount, a standalone short value still masked,
and a long value still masked verbatim.

```
$ ./venv/bin/python
title: redact: short registered vault values must not eat dates, account numbers or amounts

author: ethernet8023
body:
Stable releases can now be cut from a `release/*` branch (for example `release/0.22.1`), not only from `main`.

## Problem

Cutting a stable release has two checks that the commit is on `main`: the `release.py release` entrypoint, and the Stable Release gate that runs after dispatch. A commit that exists only on `release/0.22.1` was refused at the first one, so a patch release could not be cut from a maintenance branch.

## Before / after

| Commit being released | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| On `main` | admitted | admitted |
| Only on `release/*` | refused | admitted |
| On any other branch, or unpushed | refused | refused |

## What changes

Both checks now ask one git question, built in `scripts/releases/stable.py`:

```
git for-each-ref --contains <sha> refs/remotes/<remote>/main 'refs/remotes/<remote>/release/*'
```

Empty output means the commit is on no release line and the cut is refused.

- `entrypoint.py`: fetches `main` and `release/*` before checking. The branch fetch uses `--prune` so a deleted `release/*` branch stops admitting commits. Tags are fetched in a separate call, because pruning there would delete local-only claim tags.
- `stable.py`: claim admission (`check_claim`) and final-receipt verification (`final_context`) use the same query.
- `desktop-bundled-release.yml`: the termux "previous package" ancestry check uses the same rule, so a `v0.22.2` build can use `v0.22.1` as its previous package even though that tag is only on the release branch.
- `release.py`: `--commit` help no longer says "main commit".

## What this does not do

- **Dispatch is unchanged.** Workflows still dispatch from `main`, so the rc and release builds run main's workflow code and check out the release-branch commit. A fix to release tooling must be on `main`, and on the release branch for the local `release.py` run.
- **Canary admission is unchanged.** It stays main-only.
- **No change to version derivation.** The next version is still the published stable head plus the bump. With `v0.22.0` published, `--bump patch` gives `0.22.1`.

## Things reviewers should know

1. `release/*` has no branch ruleset today (`protect-main` covers only `main`). The old check existed so only reviewed commits get built by a signing workflow. Anyone with push access can now get a build admitted by pushing to `release/*`. A ruleset for `release/*` should land before this is relied on.
2. Once `v0.22.1` is published from the release branch, it is the stable head. The next cut f
title: ci(release): admit stable releases from release/* branches, not just main

On a Windows Desktop hand-off, an update receipt may prove that no runtime was present before the update. Previously, `windows.ps1` ignored that plan and invoked `gateway start --all` unless `-NoGateway` was supplied. This change uses only the completed receipt for the hand-off's correlation ID to skip that cold start when `plan.runtimes` is explicitly empty, while unreadable, stale, and malformed receipts retain the existing restart behavior.

author: tio-plato
body:
## What does this PR do?

`_restore_plugin_prompt_sections()` only accepts the plugin-section container when it is followed directly by `\n\nConversation started:`, but `build_system_prompt_parts()` emits the active-profile paragraph (`_active_profile_line()`, never empty, the default profile included) between the two. So no persisted prompt's sections are ever recovered, and a resumed agent's frozen snapshot (`restore_plugin_prompt_sections()`, called on resume from `conversation_loop.py`) is always `()`. Two effects on a resumed agent:

- At the next rebuild boundary (`invalidate_system_prompt()`, compaction), a render that raises as a whole (e.g. plugin discovery failing) has no previous bytes to fall back on, so the plugin sections drop out of the rebuilt prompt instead of being kept. A single section whose callback raises is skipped per-section either way; this is about the whole-render fallback.
- Readers that rebuild a resumed agent's prompt parts without a rebuild boundary (`build_system_prompt_parts()`, e.g. `compute_session_context_breakdown()`) see no plugin sections.

The fix reads through exactly that one paragraph. The builder and the parser now share the paragraph's opening (`_ACTIVE_PROFILE_PREFIX`), so recovery still accepts only the container core emits: any other text between the container and the timestamp still fails recovery. Prompts persisted with the timestamp right after the container (before the profile paragraph moved into the volatile tier) still recover. The prompt bytes the builder emits do not change.

## Related Issue

No dedicated issue. Reported as a pre-existing finding in the review of #129115 ([review thread](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/129115#discussion_r4148586549), which asks for "an assertion that fails today"); the later maintainer review there confirms it is pre-existing on main. #129115 itself states it leaves this unrepaired.

Note for #129115: it appends the platform hint between the profile paragraph and the timestamp. With this PR merged first, `test_sections_are_recovered_from_the_prompt_the_builder_emits` fails on that layout, which is the intent: whichever change lands second has to extend `_past_profile_paragraph()` (or the ordering) so recovery keeps working.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `agent/system_prompt.py`: `_ACTIVE_PROFILE_PREFIX`, shared by `_active_profile_line()` (output byte-identical) and the new `_past

## Summary

The Bot Mode plugin shipped `BOTS_LOCALES = { en, ja, zh, 'zh-hant' }`, so no French user ever saw a French Bot Mode: every string fell back to the plugin's English bundle.

- `apps/desktop/src/plugins/hermes-bots/i18n.ts` — new complete `fr` bundle (399 keys, same `BotsMessages` shape, message functions and their arity included), registered in `BOTS_LOCALES`.

Deliberately left alone, following the file's own contract: model-facing prompts, cron expressions and identifiers, and the `'You'` room-log sentinel stay English; shared core vocabulary (weekdays, Daily/Hourly, generic verbs) still resolves through the core catalogue instead of being duplicated here.

## Cause

Plugin bundles carry their own locale maps, and the registry resolves active locale -> plugin `en` -> raw key. A locale that is missing from the map is not an error, it is silently English — which is how Bot Mode shipped with no French at all.

Add the complete French bundle. A locale-completeness bench that keeps every shipped plugin locale in step with English lands with the Kanban PR (`apps/desktop/src/i18n/plugin-locale-completeness.test.ts`); it covers this bundle too, in either merge order.

Refs #136707.

The holographic provider's `is_available()` returns **True even without numpy** (SQLite alone works), but without numpy its HRR kernel silently redistributes weights to FTS-only (`hrr_weight` 0.3 → 0.0) and facts get no `hrr_vector`. The reporter's container deployment ran degraded for weeks with green logs and **no surface reporting it**. This PR adds that surface — the observability slice of the issue only.

- `hermes_cli/memory_provider_health.py` (new): reads the HRR kernel's own `_HAS_NUMPY` flag from the **loaded** provider package. Core never imports a plugin's third-party dependency itself; when the plugin build exposes no kernel flag it returns `None` and callers stay silent rather than assert a state they can't verify.
- `hermes doctor` (`doctor_state.py`): registers `holographic` in the previously-empty `_MEMORY_PROVIDER_CHECKS` per-provider table. numpy present → `✓ HRR semantic recall active (numpy x.y.z)`; missing → `⚠ holographic HRR recall degraded (numpy missing)` plus a manual-issue line in the doctor summary.
- `hermes memory status` (`memory_setup.py`): one line — `HRR: semantic recall active ✓ (numpy x.y.z)` or `HRR: degraded ✗ (numpy missing — recall is FTS-only)`.

author: Schubox84
body:
## Summary

When the Desktop composer says a turn is busy but the local session-state cache says it is not live, `redirectPrompt` currently refuses before contacting the backend. On long-lived or reattached sessions, that cached slice can be stale, causing every mid-turn message to be silently queued until reload.

Before refusing on that contradictory state, probe the owning backend with `session.active_list`. Permit the redirect only when the backend confirms the captured runtime is running; ended or unknown remains a refusal. Bound this interactive probe to three seconds so a stale cache cannot hold the composer for the watchdog's full timeout.

Fixes #138581.

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Tests were not run.
- ESLint could not run: pnpm stopped at its ignored-build-scripts approval gate, and the commit-hook fallback lacked `@eslint/js`.

body:
## What does this PR do?

Holds the Desktop "While working" keep-awake blocker for 5 minutes after the last turn goes idle, so an unattended Windows machine can't sleep in the gap before a follow-up turn starts.

Stacked on #138560 (base is its branch, not `main`): that PR moves keep-awake into `keep-awake-controller.ts` and makes "While working" the default, which is why the grace now matters to every user. Re-lands #134781 on top of it.

## Related Issue

Fixes #134434

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)

## Credit

The fix and root cause are @zwmaupin's (#134781): Windows counts sleep idleness from the last user input, so releasing the blocker at end-of-turn lets an idle machine sleep within seconds. Commit 1 is her commit, authorship kept, with its `main.ts` hunks re-applied inside the controller (her `main.ts` code no longer exists after #138560). Re-landed from an `origin` branch because her fork PR has not had CI.

## Changes Made

- `power-save.ts`: `KEEP_AWAKE_RELEASE_GRACE_MS` (5 min).
- `keep-awake-controller.ts`: in `while-working`, `apply()` re-arms a one-shot timer on live work and keeps the blocker held while it is pending; the timer re-reads `isWorking()` when it fires. Leaving `while-working` cancels it.
- Follow-up commit: tests drive the controller with fake timers. It also drops the pure `keepAwakeHeld` (hold = `keepAwakeWanted || grace armed`), arms the timer only in `while-working`, and deletes a test that asserted a constant against itself.
- Mapping commit: `contributors/emails/` entry for zwmaupin's noreply email.

## How to Test

1. `cd apps/desktop && env -u NODE_ENV npx vitest run electron/keep-awake-controller.test.ts electron/power-save.test.ts` (14 pass).
2. Set keep-awake to "While working", end a turn: the blocker stays held for 5 min, and a chained follow-up does not restart it.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| vitest (controller + power-save) | 14/14 pass |
| `tsc --build tsconfig.electron.json`, eslint, prettier | clean |
| `scripts/check --only health` | ok |
| Mutants: drop grace term / drop re-arm on work / drop cancel outside `while-working` | one test red each |
| Real Windows machine, real app | **not run** |

Not covered: bg-review and compression runs longer than 5 min (needs backend phase reporting; same non-goal as #134781).

author: Schubox84
body:
## Summary

Discord can append `(The user sent a message with no text content)` to a voice-note turn that already contains a transcript. That marker is transport scaffolding, not part of the user's topic, but title generation currently sends it to both the instant title path and the auxiliary model. The model can then save titles such as “Empty message greeting” with `llm` provenance, preventing later title upgrades.

Strip this exact marker while preparing title-only text. The transcript remains available to title both stages; placeholder-only messages reduce to empty and are not titleable.

Fixes #138573.

## Validation

- `ruff check agent/title_generator.py`
- `git diff --check`

Tests were not run.

author: JoaoMarcos44
body:
## What does this PR do?

On Python 3.11–3.13, `import tui_gateway.methods_onboarding` raises `NameError: name 'Path' is not defined` at `_shared_nous_store() -> tuple[Path, ...]`. `tui_gateway/server.py` imports that split module while installing handlers, so the TUI / Desktop backend never loads. Python 3.14 (PEP 649) hides the same crash at import time.

This PR:

1. Imports `Path` in `methods_onboarding.py` — it is a real runtime name (`Path(...)` at the due-stamp and unfinished-run helpers), matching sibling handlers such as `methods_bot_relay.py`.
2. Closes the **class** hole that let this ship: ruff F821 is excluded for all of `tui_gateway/*` because `bind_module` injects *body* names (`_ok`, `_err`, `_sessions`). Annotations still evaluate in the split module at `def` time when the file has no `from __future__ import annotations`. New rule **HX014** flags those unbound annotation names in `bind_module` modules.

## Related Issue

Fixes #138516

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Investigation

- Issue: https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/138516
- Baseline: `origin/main` `c5fc0958b49f415041c7f356c8bdf9f914037e89`
- Mechanism: `tui_gateway/methods_onboarding.py:71` `def _shared_nous_store() -> tuple[Path, ...]`. No `from pathlib import Path`, no `from __future__ import annotations`.
- Why CI missed it: `scripts/code_health/config.py` excludes `tui_gateway/*` from F821. That is correct for rebound *bodies*. It is wrong for *annotations*, which `bind_module` never rewrites.
- Sibling scan: 18 `bind_module` modules lack postponed annotations. After the Path import, HX014 reports 0 hits on those files. Nested `Document` in `methods_complete.py` is defined after a local import inside a handler (not import-time). The 30 postponed modules are out of this crash class.

## Root cause

Split onboarding handlers were extracted with a `Path` annotation and runtime `Path(...)` calls, but without importing `Path`. `bind_module` rebinds bytecode globals onto `server.py` after import, so a static reading of the calls looks fine. The annotation is evaluated first.

The **class** cause is the F821 exclude covering annotation names that the seam does not inject.

## Solution

- Instance: `from pathlib import Path` in `methods_onboarding.py`.
- Class: HX014 — in `tui_gateway` files that call `bind_module` and do not postpone annotations, every `Name` in a module-level (or class-level) function annotation must b
title: fix(tui): import Path and flag unbound split-module annotations (HX014)
